articles.summary: Ellen and Ben are on location with the London City Lionesses and Spain defender!
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 09 Nov 2026 , · 47 mins

Ellen White and Ben Haines take the pod on the road to the home of the ‘WSL disruptors’, London City Lionesses! They’re joined by special guest Jana Fernandez to discuss London City's massive shift in mindset this season, growing their fanbase, and her own impressive form. Plus, the Spanish defender reveals who she’s battling with in fiery training sessions ahead of their blockbuster WSL clash against Arsenal this weekend. Ben catches up with Jana's LCL teammate Alexia Putellas following her historic third Ballon d’Or win and to wrap up, Ellen and Ben preview two massive top-of-the-table clashes that could shake up the title race! TIMECODES: 00:05 - Ellen and Ben take the pod on the road. 02:43 - Jana Fernandez joins the pod! 05:11 - The mentality shift at London City this year. 14:00 - Building a fanbase. 18:30 - Looking at LCL’s upcoming fixtures. 21:22 - Jana on how her season is going personally and fiery training sessions. 28:50 - Daniëlle van de Donk’s form this season and Jana’s Spanish connections in London. 32:15 - Ellen and Ben reflect on their chat with Jana. 35:15 - Ben catches up with Alexia Putellas after her third Ballon d’Or win. 40:40 - Ben and Ellen debrief other WSL fixtures with two top of the table clashes ahead.

articles.title: Jacaré é encontrado na faixa de areia de praia no litoral de SP; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal foi visto na Praia da Barra do Una, em Peruíbe (SP), e chamou a atenção de moradores. Segundo a prefeitura, a espécie é nativa da região e a orientação é manter distância e não tentar tocar ou espantar o jacaré.
articles.summary: Animal foi visto na Praia da Barra do Una, em Peruíbe (SP), e chamou a atenção de moradores. Segundo a prefeitura, a espécie é nativa da região e a orientação é manter distância.
articles.body:
Um jacaré foi encontrado na faixa de areia da Praia da Barra do Una, em Peruíbe , no litoral de São Paulo. A cena chamou a atenção de moradores e foi compartilhada nas redes sociais (assista acima).

O g1 apurou que o jacaré foi encontrado no domingo (8) por Mateus Ribeiro Carvalho, proprietário de uma área de camping. Segundo ele, apesar de os moradores conhecerem a presença desses animais silvestres na região, encontros como esse não são comuns, principalmente durante o dia.

O morador explicou que, ocasionalmente, alguns jacarés saem do estuário devido à movimentação da maré vazante e acabam chegando à faixa de areia da praia.

O jacaré-de-papo-amarelo é visto na região da Barra do Una em Peruíbe (SP). — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Ainda segundo Carvalho, o animal estava camuflado na vegetação, mas foi identificado por causa do tamanho. Após perceberem que se tratava de apenas um jacaré e que não havia outros animais nas proximidades, um grupo de moradores realizou a remoção e o conduziu de volta ao rio.

“Foi uma experiência muito marcante e, ao mesmo tempo, um privilégio poder observar um animal como esse tão de perto. Mais do que o encontro em si, foi muito gratificante ter a oportunidade de contribuir para que ele voltasse ao seu habitat natural”, disse ele.

O morador também destacou a importância de respeitar e preservar a fauna local. Para ele, os animais fazem parte do ecossistema e situações como essa exigem responsabilidade, considerando tanto a segurança das pessoas quanto o bem-estar da vida silvestre.

Jacaré é encontrado na faixa de areia de praia no litoral de SP — Foto: Mateus Ribeiro Carvalho

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Peruíbe informou, por meio da Secretaria de Meio Ambiente, que o jacaré-de-papo-amarelo ( Caiman latirostris ) é uma espécie nativa da região, encontrada em rios, manguezais e outros ambientes aquáticos.

A administração municipal explicou que, como o Rio Una desemboca diretamente na praia, é possível que os animais sejam vistos nas proximidades da foz, inclusive na faixa de areia, onde podem permanecer para descansar e se aquecer ao sol.

A prefeitura ressaltou que a presença do animal em seu ambiente natural não representa, por si só, uma situação que exija resgate. A orientação é manter distância, não tentar tocar, alimentar ou espantar o jacaré.

A intervenção dos órgãos competentes deve ocorrer quando houver risco efetivo às pessoas ou ao próprio animal.

articles.title: Trump: FBI investiga espionagem em caso de traição por CEO da Nvidia | G1
articles.standfirst: Jensen Huang admitiu relacionamento extraconjugal com mulher suspeita de repassar informações para a China. Segundo Trump, empresário afirmou que não sabia da atuação dela como espiã.
articles.summary: Jensen Huang admitiu relacionamento extraconjugal com mulher suspeita de repassar informações para a China. Segundo Trump, empresário afirmou que não sabia da atuação dela como espiã.
articles.body:
Após o CEO da Nvidia , Jensen Huang, admitir ter traído a esposa em meio a suspeitas de um esquema de espionagem, o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , afirmou que o caso será investigado pelo FBI .

Trump disse ter conversado com Huang nesta segunda-feira (9) sobre uma reportagem de outubro em que o jornal The New York Times ligou o executivo a uma empresária acusada de repassar informações sigilosas para a China.

Segundo Trump, Huang disse que não sabia que a mulher era uma espiã. "Eu realmente acredito nele", disse o republicano. "Eu sei que o FBI está investigando. Ele ficará em uma situação confortável".

A fabricante de chips Nvidia disse no domingo (8) que abriu uma investigação independente para apurar se Huang foi alvo de uma operação de inteligência estrangeira. Segundo a empresa, o executivo apoia a apuração e se comprometeu a colaborar com o processo.

Ainda segundo o jornal, Trump foi informado sobre as suspeitas há cerca de um ano, mas não adotou nenhuma medida porque o governo temia que uma reação prejudicasse os negócios da Nvidia e a relação entre os EUA e a China.

Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, ao lado de Donald Trump, presidente dos Estados Unidos, em foto de 8 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Reuters/Evan Vucci

De lavador de pratos a bilionário: conheça o CEO da Nvidia

Em mensagem enviada a funcionários, Huang admitiu o relacionamento extraconjugal e disse ter "total responsabilidade" por seus atos. "Fui infiel à minha esposa. Minhas ações fizeram mal a ela e aos nossos filhos. Não há desculpa para o que fiz", disse.

Huang é um dos aliados mais próximos de Trump no Vale do Silício. Ele demonstrou apoio à agenda do governo americano nos últimos dois anos e se tornou presença constante em Washington pelo desejo da Nvidia de vender seus chips para o mercado chinês.

Segundo o jornal The New York Times, Huang teve um relacionamento com Alice Huang, ex-executiva da Megaspeed, empresa de data centers sediada em Singapura.

Apesar do sobrenome em comum, ela não tem parentesco com Jensen Huang.

Autoridades dos EUA investigaram o caso e concluíram que ela atuava como agente da inteligência chinesa .

Alice Huang trabalhou como repórter de televisão na China antes de se tornar uma das principais executivas da Megaspeed, que se tornou uma das maiores clientes da Nvidia no Sudeste Asiático.

Segundo o NYT, a Megaspeed comprou mais de US$ 4,8 bilhões em chips da Nvidia nos últimos dois anos .

A própria Megaspeed foi investigada por autoridades americanas, por suspeitas de que tenha ajudado Pequim a obter acesso a chips avançados de inteligência artificial, cuja exportação para a China é proibida .

➡️ Desde 2022, os Estados Unidos mantêm controles de exportação destinados a restringir o acesso da China aos chips avançados da Nvidia e aos equipamentos necessários para produzi-los.

A carta do CEO da Nvidia aos funcionários não mencionou Alice Huang nem tratou de suas aparentes ligações com Pequim.

Huang, no entanto, fez referência às preocupações de segurança nacional levantadas pelas reportagens e afirmou que apoia e cooperará integralmente com a investigação do conselho.

Anteriormente, no fim de outubro, o CEO havia dito à Bloomberg News que sua relação com Alice Huang eram "completamente normais e nada incomuns".

A Megaspeed informou que sua atual liderança leva o assunto a sério e contratou advogados externos para conduzir uma investigação interna. Alice Huang não respondeu aos pedidos de comentário.

articles.title: COP31: ONU afirma que países precisam fazer mais para conter aquecimento do planeta | G1
articles.standfirst: Antália, no sul da Turquia, vai sediar a cúpula de líderes globais. A presidência é compartilhada com a Austrália, responsável pela construção da agenda técnica do encontro.
articles.summary: Antália, no sul da Turquia, vai sediar a cúpula de líderes globais. A presidência é compartilhada com a Austrália, responsável pela construção da agenda técnica do encontro.
articles.body:
A Conferência da ONU sobre o clima começou nesta segunda-feira (9) na Turquia em meio a novos alertas sobre o aquecimento do planeta. A reportagem é dos enviados especiais Murilo Salviano, Igor Arroyo e Natalie Reinoso.

São passos pequenos, desengonçados. Mas, sem persistência, os filhotinhos não chegariam ao mar. A tartaruga-marinha é o mascote da COP31. Um animal diretamente ameaçado pelo aquecimento do planeta e que, por instinto, entende o caminho da vida.

Em um ritmo parecido avançam as negociações do clima. Desta vez em Antália, no sul da Turquia, que vai sediar a cúpula de líderes globais, que começa nesta segunda-feira (9). A presidência é compartilhada com a Austrália , responsável pela construção da agenda técnica do encontro.

Uma das principais apostas desta COP é a eletrificação da economia. A proposta é substituir parte do consumo de combustíveis fósseis - como a combustão dos carros, que vem da gasolina e do diesel - por energia produzida a partir de fontes mais limpas, como o sol e o vento. Os negociadores querem subir a proporção global de energia elétrica de 23% para 35% até 2035.

Nesta segunda-feira (9), na passagem oficial da presidência da COP, o embaixador brasileiro André Corrêa do Lago, que comandou a COP30, em Belém, entregou aos anfitriões um martelo feito de madeira amazônica. Em entrevista ao Jornal Nacional , o embaixador disse que o resultado das últimas eleições americanas pode influenciar parte das discussões desta conferência.

“O governo Trump está mudando a legislação americana, tirando os incentivos à transição e, muito pelo contrário, incentivando o retorno aos fósseis. Mas isso tem que passar pelo Congresso americano. Então, essa vitória democrata no Congresso vai ter um impacto gigantesco sobre a discussão de clima”, diz André Corrêa do Lago, presidente da COP30.

COP31: ONU afirma que países precisam fazer mais para conter aquecimento do planeta — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Donald Trump não enviou representantes à Turquia. Algo já esperado de um governo que retirou os Estados Unidos do Acordo de Paris, pacto firmado por mais de 190 países para limitar o aquecimento do planeta. Uma meta cada vez mais difícil de ser atingida.

Um relatório divulgado nesta segunda-feira (9) pela ONU apontou que 2026 deve ser um dos quatro anos mais quentes já registrados. A ONU afirma que os esforços feitos até aqui são insuficientes e que os países precisam fazer mais - com urgência . É nesse espírito dos negociadores que agora desembarcam na Turquia.

O documento também destaca que o super El Niño deve atingir o pico em dezembro de 2026 e provocar ainda mais transtornos climáticos. Outro obstáculo são as guerras no Irã , na Ucrânia . Conflitos que agravam a crise global de energia e que estão afetando diretamente as economias mais ricas, que têm papel decisivo no financiamento dos projetos climáticos.

“Não só nós temos que diminuir o desmatamento, mas a plantação de florestas, ou seja, você aumentar a cobertura vegetal, é a única forma, hoje, cientificamente comprovada e economicamente viável de você absorver CO2 que já foi emitido”, afirma André Corrêa do Lago.

Esse é um dos pilares do mapa do caminho entregue pela equipe brasileira para a nova presidência da COP. As propostas incluem frear o desmatamento, acelerar a redução da dependência dos combustíveis fósseis e ampliar as fontes de financiamento para a ação climática. Um mapa que indica um objetivo que parece distante, mas que insiste em apostar na caminhada.

articles.title: Após vitória de Lula, Rubio diz que EUA vão manter diálogo com Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Secretário de Estado afirmou que há divergências comerciais e em outros temas envolvendo os países. Rubio disse que pretende conversar com o chanceler brasileiro, Mauro Vieira.
articles.summary: Secretário de Estado afirmou que há divergências comerciais e em outros temas envolvendo os países. Rubio disse que pretende conversar com o chanceler brasileiro, Mauro Vieira.
articles.body:
O secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos , Marco Rubio , afirmou nesta segunda-feira (9) que o governo de Donald Trump vai continuar mantendo contato com o governo brasileiro, apesar das divergências entre os dois países. A declaração foi feita durante a reunião de chanceleres do G7, em Paris, na França.

Questionado sobre a relação entre Brasil e Estados Unidos, dias após a reeleição do presidente Lula (PT), Rubio disse que pretende conversar com o ministro das Relações Exteriores do Brasil, Mauro Vieira , sobre os próximos passos da parceria entre os dois países.

"Vamos lidar com o governo brasileiro. Já lidávamos com ele antes", afirmou o secretário.

Rubio disse ainda que tem uma boa relação com Mauro Vieira. Por outro lado, o secretário de Estado norte-americano cobrou uma solução para o impasse envolvendo a indicação de Daniel Perez para o cargo de embaixador dos Estados Unidos no Brasil.

Perez foi escolhido pelo presidente Donald Trump para representar o governo americano em Brasília.

No entanto, a indicação ainda depende da aprovação do governo brasileiro, em um procedimento diplomático conhecido como "agrément".

"Temos um problema porque eles não permitiram que nosso embaixador entrasse no país. Isso é um problema. Danny Perez é nosso indicado. Isso precisa ser resolvido", afirmou Rubio.

O secretário disse esperar que o governo brasileiro autorize a entrada do indicado e argumentou que a situação prejudica a relação entre os dois países.

"Não achamos que isso estabeleça um bom-tom para a nossa relação. Eles têm um embaixador nos Estados Unidos, mas, em algum momento, esse desequilíbrio não pode continuar", declarou.

O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, em 9 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: Brendan Smialowski/Pool via Reuters

A indicação de Perez foi feita por Trump em junho e aprovada pelo Senado dos Estados Unidos em agosto.

Pelas regras internacionais, porém, o processo só é concluído após o consentimento do país que receberá o representante diplomático. Sem essa autorização, o indicado não pode assumir oficialmente o cargo.

Segundo o blog da Ana Flor , a indicação de Perez causou mal-estar no governo brasileiro porque o anúncio foi feito antes de uma consulta reservada às autoridades brasileiras.

Tradicionalmente, a nomeação de um embaixador só é anunciada após o país anfitrião sinalizar que aceita a indicação.

No caso de Perez, o pedido de aval foi feito ao governo brasileiro mais de duas semanas após o anúncio da indicação pela Casa Branca.

Em agosto, os Estados Unidos anunciaram a revogação do visto da embaixadora do Brasil em Washington, Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti , em meio ao impasse diplomático.

Segundo o Departamento de Estado dos EUA, ela pode permanecer no país e terá o visto renovado depois que o governo brasileiro aprovar a indicação de Perez para o cargo de embaixador.

À época, o Itamaraty repudiou a decisão americana e disse que as justificativas apresentadas pelo Departamento de Estado são "falsas". O ministério disse ainda haver interesse dos EUA em interferir nas eleições brasileiras.

Como eleições nos EUA devem selar destino de Trump e futuro da relação com o Brasil em 4º mandato de Lula — Foto: Pablo PORCIUNCULA e Andrew CABALLERO-REYNOLDS / AFP via Getty Images

Rubio também mencionou questões comerciais como um dos pontos de divergência entre os governos brasileiro e americano.

Atualmente, Brasil e Estados Unidos negociam a retirada de uma série de taxas impostas pela Casa Branca contra produtos brasileiros importados pelos norte-americanos.

Embora tenha afirmado que não é o responsável direto pelas negociações comerciais, o secretário disse acompanhar de perto o assunto por considerar que as relações comerciais também afetam a política externa dos Estados Unidos.

O secretário disse ainda que existem diferenças entre as posições dos dois governos sobre outros temas, que ainda precisarão ser resolvidas.

articles.title: Professores entram em greve no Paraguai | G1
articles.standfirst: Mobilização cobra proteção a US$ 60 milhões de fundos de pensão depositados no Ueno Bank. Mais de 3 milhões de pessoas ficaram sem acesso às contas após intervenção do governo.
articles.summary: Mobilização cobra proteção a US$ 60 milhões de fundos de pensão depositados no Ueno Bank. Mais de 3 milhões de pessoas ficaram sem acesso às contas após intervenção do governo.
articles.body:
Professores da rede pública do Paraguai entraram em greve nesta segunda-feira (9) e foram às ruas de várias cidades do país. A mobilização ocorre após a quebra do banco Ueno, que provou o impeachment e a prisão do presidente Santiago Peña.

Silvio Piris, presidente da Federação de Educadores do Paraguai, afirmou que os professores estão preocupados com o destino de cerca de US$ 60 milhões (R$ 330 milhões) de fundos de pensão depositados no banco.

"Queremos que a devolução desse dinheiro seja uma prioridade", disse Piris ao Canal 9 do Paraguai.

Mais de 3 milhões de pessoas ficaram sem acesso às próprias contas bancárias na última terça-feira (3), depois que o governo do Paraguai interveio no Ueno Bank. O fechamento da instituição também afetou fundos de pensão e contas do governo.

Em entrevista coletiva no sábado (7), os promotores disseram que Peña será investigado pelos crimes de quebra de confiança e administração em benefício próprio. Se for condenado, ele poderá enfrentar até 20 anos de prisão.

O ex-presidente está detido em uma base militar enquanto as investigações continuam. Ele foi substituído pelo então vice-presidente, Pedro Alliana.

Peña também foi acusado por parlamentares de usar a influência política para direcionar centenas de milhões de dólares em recursos públicos ao Ueno.

A investigação por corrupção também envolve o ex-presidente do Banco Central do Paraguai.

As acusações que levaram à saída de Peña do cargo apontam que o ex-presidente tinha participação na empresa controladora do Ueno, da qual se desfez sob pressão no ano passado.

Ele também teria nomeado um ex-executivo do banco para comandar o Banco Central, responsável pela regulação da instituição.

Os parlamentares também acusam Peña de permitir que o fundo de pensão estatal depositasse US$ 355 milhões (R$ 1,9 bilhão) no banco, acima do limite permitido por lei. O ex-presidente nega irregularidades.

O Banco Central começou na semana passada a devolver os depósitos aos correntistas. Até sábado, segundo a instituição, mais de 1,2 milhão de clientes do Ueno haviam recebido reembolsos parciais ou integrais.

Os depósitos bancários no Paraguai têm garantia de até aproximadamente US$ 37 mil (R$ 203 mil).

A crise provocou uma série de protestos de correntistas, que terminaram em confrontos com a polícia. A situação também gerou dúvidas sobre a estabilidade do sistema financeiro paraguaio.

A moeda do país, o guarani, perdeu cerca de 8% do valor em relação ao dólar desde a intervenção no Ueno.

Policiais fazem a segurança em frente a uma agência do Banco Ueno durante um protesto de depositantes após a intervenção do Banco Central do Paraguai no banco, em Assunção, em 3 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: Daniel Duarte/AFP

articles.title: Papa Leão XIV reúne mais de 2,5 milhões de fiéis em Buenos Aires | G1
articles.standfirst: Fazia 39 anos que um papa não visitava a Argentina.
articles.summary: Fazia 39 anos que um papa não visitava a Argentina.
articles.body:
A viagem do Papa Leão XIV pela América do Sul levou nesta segunda-feira (9) uma multidão às ruas de Buenos Aires . Mais de 2,5 milhões de fiéis se reuniram para uma missa no segundo dia da visita à Argentina . O correspondente Raphael Sibilla esteve na Catedral Metropolitana de Buenos Aires:

"Nesse momento, o Papa Leão XIV está participando de um jantar com bispos na residência oficial do arcebispo de Buenos Aires, que fica aqui ao lado da Catedral Metropolitana. Como vocês podem ver, ainda há algumas pessoas em frente à catedral, porque, agora há pouco, o papa participou da celebração das Vésperas com o episcopado e quebrou o protocolo: de improviso, de uma sacada, discursou para os fiéis presentes. Fazia 39 anos que um papa não visitava a Argentina, desde João Paulo II, e a presença dele tem emocionado os argentinos pelas atitudes e pelas palavras. Ele tem ressaltado o valor da família, a importância dos jovens e falado de justiça social, destacando a importância dos governos em cuidar dos mais necessitados. O antecessor, o Papa Francisco, primeiro papa latino-americano e amigo de Leão XIV, tem sido lembrado em quase todos os discursos. E nesta segunda-feira, uma multidão acompanhou os compromissos do pontífice aqui na Argentina".

Uma espera que começou de madrugada. Um argentino acordou às 3h30 para aguardar o Papa Leão XIV e disse que, quando chegou, já tinha muita gente. A voluntária foi para ajudar os outros fiéis a viverem este momento histórico.

Papa Leão XIV reúne mais de 2,5 milhões de fiéis em Buenos Aires — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

No segundo dia de visitas ao país, o pontífice esteve muito próximo dos fiéis. Rodou mais de 50 km, sempre acompanhado por multidões. Esteve em uma instituição de caridade que atende mais de 400 pessoas com deficiência. Se emocionou ao escutar as palavras de Marta, uma senhora que vive no local. Afirmou, mais uma vez, que é papel do governo cuidar dos mais necessitados. No discurso, Leão XIV disse que a vida das pessoas atendidas em instituições não são um peso para a sociedade, mas uma bênção:

“Elas nos ajudam a não esquecer qual é o fundamento da dignidade de cada ser humano e o que realmente é importante na vida”.

O evento mais esperado do dia lotou o bairro de Palermo, na capital argentina. Uma multidão reunida para acompanhar a missa celebrada pelo pontífice - inclusive o presidente Javier Milei . Brasileiras que estudam Medicina na Argentina tiveram a sorte de estar perto do papa.

“Vai ficar marcado para as nossas vidas inteiras”, diz a estudante.

“A gente está, assim, extremamente emocionada. Às vezes, dá vontade até de chorar, de sentir que ele está tão pertinho da gente”, conta outra estudante.

Durante a homilia, Leão XIV falou sobre situações que cada família enfrenta: falta de estabilidade, dificuldades sociais, trabalho precário, violência doméstica, separações dolorosas e vícios que destroem o futuro dos jovens e deterioram relações familiares. O papa pediu para que os lares dos argentinos sejam a porta de entrada da Igreja para a juventude.

Neste segundo dia de Leão XIV à Argentina, mais de 2,5 milhões de pessoas saíram de casa nesta segunda-feira (9) em Buenos Aires . Fazia 39 anos que um papa não visitava o país. E novamente, durante a missa, Leão XIV fez questão de relembrar do antecessor argentino, o Papa Francisco, que faleceu em 2025. Uma fiel diz que se emociona quando o papa fala sobre Francisco:

“Foi ele quem nos deu mais visibilidade, nos deu mais oportunidades de crescer na Igreja”.

“É sentir que o legado de Francisco segue vivo”, disse outra mulher.

Após a missa, o papa se encontrou com trabalhadores na Universidade Católica Argentina. Criticou o que chamou de inteligência artificial desregulada, que, segundo o papa, pode se tornar uma ameaça ao desenvolvimento humano. Disse que o algoritmo não pode substituir o discernimento humano nem o valor da presencialidade e do esforço do trabalhador.

Nesta segunda-feira (9), o pontífice vai viajar para o interior do país e celebrará uma missa em Córdoba, segunda maior cidade argentina.

articles.title: Chuvas fortes reduzem produção de trigo e Brasil terá que aumentar em 20% a importação do cereal para atender demanda interna | G1
articles.standfirst: O pãozinho de cada dia está na ponta da cadeia produtiva do trigo. Mas o consumidor não deve sentir diferença no preço até o fim de 2026, segundo a associação brasileira que representa a indústria de panificação.
articles.summary: O pãozinho de cada dia está na ponta da cadeia produtiva do trigo. Mas o consumidor não deve sentir diferença no preço até o fim de 2026, segundo a associação brasileira que representa a indústria de panificação.
articles.body:
As chuvas fortes reduziram a produção de trigo no Brasil e o país vai ter que aumentar em 20% a importação de trigo para atender a demanda interna.

Pode não parecer, mas você está vendo uma das piores safras que a terra já colheu. E o motivo caiu do céu.

“A gente teve um desafio climático extremamente grande na época, no período de colheita, em função desse excesso de chuva”, conta o produtor rural Frederik Wolters.

O produtor de trigo do interior de São Paulo investiu, mas a produtividade despencou 20%. Os grãos ainda perderam qualidade.

“Um trigo tipo 1, que era destinado para a produção de pão, massas no geral, ele perde a qualidade de panificação dele e ele se torna um trigo voltado para ração”, diz Frederik Wolters.

Na reta final de safra, os temporais na Região Sul também levaram embora o esforço de meses nas lavouras. A produção brasileira não deve chegar a 6 milhões de toneladas. Uma queda de 27% em relação ao ciclo passado. Metade do trigo que a gente precisa já vem de importação. Mas, em 2026, o Brasil terá que comprar pelo menos 20% a mais.

“Nós estamos tendo, neste ano, que fazer uma importação recorde. Nos últimos 30 anos, não houve nunca um momento em que o Brasil teve que importar quase 10 milhões de toneladas para atender o consumo interno. Nós estamos, realmente, vivendo um momento muito desafiador para todo o setor, para a cadeia do trigo", afirma Rubens Barbosa, presidente da Abitrigo.

Chuvas fortes reduzem produção de trigo e Brasil terá que aumentar em 20% a importação do cereal para atender a demanda interna — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O problema é que o trigo está disputado no mercado internacional. A Argentina , nossa maior fornecedora, também enfrenta problemas climáticos, e a maior exportadora, a Rússia , está com dificuldades de escoar a produção por causa da guerra com a Ucrânia. Na cotação internacional, o preço disparou. Em setembro, atingiu o maior valor em três anos.

O pãozinho de cada dia está na ponta da cadeia produtiva do trigo. O consumidor não deve sentir diferença no preço até o fim de 2026, segundo a associação brasileira que representa a indústria de panificação. Por enquanto, o setor foi orientado a absorver os impactos.

O economista especializado em agro explica que o trigo é um produto que pode ser estocado, o que permite contornar um pouco a alta de preços. Mas nem tudo pode ser controlado.

“A primeira parte da economia que é afetada é justamente a agricultura dentro de eventos climáticos extremos, como o El Niño que a gente está vivendo agora. E, às vezes, não tem como a gente fazer trocas tão fáceis assim. Por exemplo, o trigo é muito difícil a gente substituir por um outro produto”, diz Leandro Gilio, professor do Insper Agro Global.

articles.title: Trump cita dia ruim com imprensa ao explicar piada sobre chefe do UFC | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente afirmou no domingo (8) que proposta a empresário era uma piada. Durante briefing, também comentou conflitos no Irã e na Ucrânia.
articles.summary: Presidente afirmou no domingo que proposta a empresário era uma piada. Durante briefing, também comentou conflitos no Irã e na Ucrânia.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , admitiu nesta segunda-feira (9) que inventou o convite ao presidente do UFC, Dana White, para assumir o cargo de porta-voz da Casa Branca porque estava tendo um "dia muito ruim" com a imprensa.

A declaração foi feita durante um briefing na Casa Branca, que contou com a presença de White. Trump apresentou o empresário aos jornalistas e voltou a brincar sobre a possibilidade de ele assumir o cargo.

Segundo o presidente, até a atual porta-voz, Karoline Leavitt, concordaria que o chefe do UFC seria uma boa escolha. Trump, no entanto, disse que havia um problema: White poderia acabar partindo para a agressão física contra os jornalistas.

"Ele vai falar por um tempo e depois vai bater em vocês", brincou Trump.

Ao final da coletiva, Trump perguntou diretamente a White se ele gostaria de assumir o cargo de secretário de imprensa. White agradeceu a oferta, mas recusou: "Não quero me envolver com política".

Na sequência, Trump disse, em tom de brincadeira, que estava "arrasado" com a decisão.

O CEO do UFC, Dana White, reage enquanto o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, discursa na Sala de Imprensa da Casa Branca — Foto: REUTERS/Aaron Schwartz

Em publicação no Truth Social, no sábado (7), Trump havia dito que convidou White para ser o secretário de Imprensa da Casa Branca . No mesmo post, ele pediu que o empresário levasse integrantes do mundo das lutas para trabalhar como assistentes.

Entre os nomes mencionados estava o da brasileira Amanda Nunes, ex-campeã considerada uma das maiores lutadoras da história do MMA.

No dia seguinte , Trump afirmou que estava "apenas brincando" sobre o convite feito a White. Segundo o presidente, o empresário "adorou a ideia", mas a sugestão não era séria.

White está à frente do UFC há mais de duas décadas e é um aliado próximo de Trump.

Ele também ajudou a mobilizar apoio para a campanha presidencial do republicano em 2024.

O empresário apareceu ao lado de Trump em diversos eventos políticos e ajudou a levar eventos do UFC para o gramado da Casa Branca neste ano.

O cargo de porta-voz da Casa Branca está vago desde 16 de outubro, quando Katie Zacharia deixou a função após apenas cinco dias no posto . Ela realizou uma única entrevista coletiva, que durou cerca de 14 minutos e recebeu críticas pela condução.

Zacharia havia sido escolhida para substituir Karoline Leavitt, que se afastou em agosto após dar à luz a segunda filha. Desde então, integrantes do governo se revezaram nas entrevistas coletivas.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, conversa com jornalistas na Casa Branca em 9 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: Aaron Schwartz/Reuters

Durante o briefing desta segunda-feira, Trump também comentou os conflitos no Oriente Médio e na Ucrânia.

Sobre o Irã, o presidente afirmou que os Estados Unidos estão vendo um avanço positivo em direção ao fim do conflito e que, neste momento, uma ação militar não parece necessária.

Trump disse ainda que teve uma "excelente conversa" com o primeiro-ministro do Catar. Ele afirmou que os Estados Unidos estão "prontos para agir" caso haja alguma mudança nos acontecimentos no Oriente Médio, mas avaliou que essa possibilidade parece bastante improvável neste momento.

Sobre a guerra entre Rússia e Ucrânia, o republicano afirmou que houve uma "conversa muito boa" sobre o conflito durante uma reunião em Abu Dhabi. O encontro contou com a presença de autoridades russas, ucranianas e americanas.

articles.title: Data Blackout: Likely Diwali AQI in Delhi higher than 370
articles.summary: Delhi saw major AQI data outages during Diwali peak hours; TOI estimates air quality may have exceeded 370 vs official 344, raising monitoring reliability concerns.
articles.body: DELHI: For the second Diwali in a row, the mysterious disappearance of data from air quality monitoring stations across Delhi during peak pollution hours has raised questions about the reliability of the govt’s AQI figures.The official average AQI of 344 on Monday makes this the second-cleanest Diwali on record among years when the day after the festival fell in Nov. But the picture changes significantly when the missing data is factored in.TOI’s calculations show that the average AQI could have exceeded 370 had the large-scale data outage not occurred, with all other factors remaining unchanged.Three aspects of the outage, which began on Sunday night, stand out.First, data from the previous day shows no disruption on anything approaching the scale witnessed on Diwali night, according to hourly AQI readings downloaded from the CPCB website, which provides station-wise data for the city.Second, most of the outage occurred between 10pm on Diwali night and 10am on Monday, when air quality was at its worst because of firecracker emissions.Of the 43 monitoring stations that reported missing data for at least an hour, 39 went off the grid after their readings had touched the maximum AQI of 500. 38 of these stations were still recording an AQI of 500 when data transmission resumed.A total of 247 hours of data went missing during this 12-hour window, averaging more than four hours for each of Delhi’s 59 monitoring stations. Outside this period, after 10am on Monday, the total data loss was barely 14 hours.Third, 12 monitoring stations recorded data outages of nine hours or more, crossing the threshold beyond which a station is excluded from the calculation of the city’s daily average AQI.Hourly readings from all 12 stations show that they were recording an AQI of 500 when the outage began and continued to do so when data transmission resumed.The only exception was the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium station, which recorded an AQI of 403, still in the ‘severe’ category, when transmission resumed at 10am after a nine-hour gap.This suggests that readings at these stations would likely have remained at or near 500 had there been no interruption in data transmission. Extrapolating from the available readings, the average AQI for the 12 stations excluded from the citywide calculation works out to 403, indicating that they were among the worst-affected pollution hotspots.Similar extrapolations for stations with shorter data outages during peak pollution hours suggest that as many as 13 monitoring stations may have recorded 24-hour average AQI levels in the ‘severe’ category, compared with just one in the official figures. Another eight stations are likely to have recorded AQI levels above 390, close to the severe threshold.It must be emphasised that these calculations are indicative estimates intended to account for substantial gaps in the available data. articles.title: Judge denies motion to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case
articles.summary: The ruling means the case can move forward, possibly with reduced charges in a new trial.
articles.body:
A Massachusetts judge has denied a motion to dismiss the murder case against Lindsay Clancy, the US woman accused of killing her three children.

The judge's ruling follows her defence team's request to dismiss the case after the 12-person jury in her September trial failed to reach a verdict.

Clancy has not denied killing her children in 2023, but her defence team argues she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time. Prosecutors say the killings were intentional.

The ruling clears the way for prosecutors to pursue the case. They could reduce the charges in a potential second trial or dismiss them altogether.

Clancy's defence team argued to dismiss the case against her due to double jeopardy - a legal standard that prevents a person from being tried for the same crime twice.

Her lawyers argued that Judge William Sullivan, who presided over the 26-day jury trial last summer, acted prematurely when he declared a mistrial on 4 September, saying that he should have sought a viable alternative.

The five-week trial, its lead-up and aftermath gripped Americans, and put postpartum mental health issues such as psychosis in the spotlight.

In his ruling on Monday, Sullivan said that a retrial would not unconstitutionally subject Clancy to double jeopardy, according to court documents obtained by the BBC.

The possibility that "an unreasonably stubborn or eccentric juror" could be seated is "an unavoidable risk of the jury system", he said.

"Because the court concludes that there was manifest necessity for a mistrial based on the jury's deadlock, a retrial on the murder indictments does not violate Clancy's right not to be placed in double jeopardy."

Sullivan also denied a defence motion to see records of the lone holdout juror in the case and to question the juror under oath.

He said the defence failed to demonstrate that the records were needed for Clancy's defence at any retrial, and that questioning the juror "would have been impermissibly coercive".

The judge has marked 16 November to discuss scheduling a potential second trial. He previously suggested it could begin in March.

The BBC has contacted Clancy's lawyers for comment.

Lindsay Clancy's ex-husband says he forgave her so he would not be 'eaten up inside forever'

Lindsay Clancy's trial puts postpartum psychosis in the spotlight

Prosecutors in the closely watched case alleged that on 24 January 2023, Clancy intentionally strangled all of her children - Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, eight months - in their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home.

After weeks of emotional testimony, the jury took a week to deliberate, repeatedly telling the judge that they could not reach a verdict.

The deadlock stemmed from a lone juror who voted to convict Clancy of first-degree murder, while the 11 other jurors intended to acquit Clancy by reason of insanity.

In Massachusetts, as well as in all US criminal murder trials, juries must reach a unanimous decision to convict or acquit a defendant.

Because the jurors failed to unanimously agree on whether the prosecution had proved Clancy was guilty "beyond a reasonable doubt" as required by US law, the judge declared a mistrial on 4 September, which means that she was neither found guilty nor not guilty.

Clancy is currently being housed in a state-run psychiatric hospital and medical facility in Massachusetts.

articles.title: Chinese nationals stream from poor localities of Dhaka, claim those are in Delhi: Report
articles.summary: The setting is Dhaka, but the audience in China is told it is Delhi.
articles.body: The setting is Dhaka, but the audience in China is told it is Delhi. An estimated total of over 150 Chinese nationals have been livestreaming from an underprivileged neighbourhood in Dhaka, falsely presenting it to their viewers back home as everyday life in India, an investigation by the Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo revealed.Equipped with two smartphones each - one used to stream live and the other with scripts - they broadcast from early morning until late at night. According to the report, the streamers focus on Sector 12 and Tekpara, which are dense, low-income settlements along a canal in Uttara town, located north of Dhaka, where they film along the tin-roofed houses. Local guides, hired for Tk 700 to Tk 800 (Rs 525-Rs 600) a day, assist the Chinese nationals in navigating the area.While most of these creators refused to speak to Prothom Alo, some only gave their names and nationality. A Chinese national named Fangyou, after being persuaded by a guide, said that such streams are broadcast on China-based platforms such as WeChat and Douyin (the mainland version of TikTok) as "part of product promotion activities".Google translations of their commentary, verified by four Bangladeshis who know Chinese, revealed misrepresentation. In one instance, a Chinese woman identifying herself as Mianmian showed the tin huts and said, "This is Delhi. Their homes are extremely dirty... and the law-and-order situation is poor."At a bridge flanked by tea stalls, another creator named Wang Wei could be heard telling his audience that locals were drinking "cow urine tea" prepared with contaminated river water. Some streamers claimed they were Chinese women married to Indian men living in these neighbourhoods, while promoting Chinese air conditioner brands seen on building walls.The continuous broadcasts have sparked anger among residents over violations of privacy. Locals, who talked to Prothom Alo, said that streamers routinely enter homes unannounced, sometimes even filming into bathrooms. When residents protest, the streamers apologise and leave, only to return soon after.Despite months of complaints from residents, the police have not monitored or regulated this activity. Mohammad Khalid Mansur, officer-in-charge of Uttara West Police Station, told Prothom Alo that officers were aware of the filming but attempts to pursue the matter have been hindered due to language barriers.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: Thicker, crispier bacon and a richer, creamier Frosty are among the menu upgrades Wendy's is testing as the Ohio-based fast-food chain launches a multiyear turnaround strategy following seven consecutive quarters of declining sales. Wendy's U.S. same-restaurant sales fell 5.7% in the third quarter of 2026, which ended Sept. 27, compared with the same period in 2025. International same-restaurant sales fell 2.2% year over year, according to the company's financial report. REGIONAL BURGER CHAINS ARE BEATING FAST-FOOD GIANTS IN ONE KEY MEASURE In an effort to "return Wendy's to sustainable growth," the chain is rolling out the "Dave's Way" plan, built around five strategic pillars: menu, marketing, operations, digital experience and "restaurants as the engine for growth," Bob Wright, Wendy's president and CEO, said in a video accompanying the announcement. In the Nov. 5 announcement, Wright called Wendy's the "quality leader" in quick-service restaurants that is "always worth what you pay." As part of the "Dave's Way" plan, the company is revamping its menu, working to improve quality and value for customers. The chain has started testing improvements to core menu items, incorporating thicker, crispier bacon, upgraded salads, a richer, creamier Frosty and whole-leaf lettuce on sandwiches, the company confirmed to Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Another key aspect of the plan is removing "lower volume items that add complexity" in Wendy's kitchens, Wright said. Franchisees will also be allowed to stop serving breakfast if they feel it does not support the restaurant's economics, according to the quarterly earnings call. A new menu board design is also being implemented in an effort to highlight signature offerings. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Since its founding in 1969 by Dave Thomas, Wendy's has become a key player in the quick-service restaurant space, now operating more than 7,000 restaurants worldwide. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS With an emphasis on fresh beef and quality ingredients, Wendy's is home to classic menu items like the Frosty and the Baconator. The new strategy comes after Wendy's rejected a $1.4 billion buyout offer from ​Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management, FOX Business reported. "We have moved quickly to align the Wendy's system to support the strategy, organize our leadership and teams around our priorities and put resources behind execution," Wright said in the announcement. articles.title: In 2008, a Massachusetts couple bought oceanfront land to build a house, but neighbours repeatedly disrupted the construction; 18 years later, an appeals court upheld a $3.7 million verdict against them
articles.summary: An Indiana couple ran several rental homes, but during divorce the husband moved $62,000 to an account his wife could not access; an appeals court upheld
articles.body: An Indiana couple ran several rental homes, but during divorce the husband moved $62,000 to an account his wife could not access; an appeals court upheld her 55% share of the marital estate and a $138,219 paymentAn Indiana couple who built a portfolio of rental homes during their marriage saw their divorce end with an unequal division of assets after the husband moved $62,000 from a joint account into an account his wife could not access. The Indiana Court of Appeals upheld the trial court’s decision to award Nichole McIntosh 55 percent of the marital estate, along with a $138,219.45 property settlement payment from Vernon McIntosh, according to the appellate decision published by Justia U.S. Law.The case shows how a divorce involving rental properties can become complicated when one spouse controls the money, the records and the day-to-day management. The appellate court found that the husband’s conduct before and during the divorce, including moving funds, concealing a coin-based transaction and failing to document rental expenses, justified treating the property division differently from a simple 50-50 split.A marriage built around rentalsVernon and Nichole McIntosh married in May 2008 and had no children together. During the marriage, they acquired several properties in Marion County, including a duplex, three single-family homes and their jointly owned marital residence on Woodlawn Avenue. All of the properties except the Woodlawn home were used as rentals, listed on Airbnb, Hospitable and through private leases. Both spouses had administrative rights and responsibilities on the rental platforms and were active in managing the properties.The couple also formed two LLCs, Zoe Rentals LLC and Shelby Home Rentals LLC, for the rental business. However, they never transferred the rental properties or mortgages into those entities, which meant the assets and debts remained tied directly to the marriage.The $62,000 transfer that changed thingsIn September 2022, just days before Vernon filed for divorce, he transferred $62,000 from a joint bank account on which Nichole was the primary owner and he was an authorized user. The money went into an account where he was the primary owner and Nichole’s access was terminated.The trial court found that this transfer was part of a broader pattern of dissipation. Vernon also eliminated Nichole’s administrative access to the Airbnb portal, reported credit cards on which she was a joint user as stolen, used a marital credit card to pay $4,800 to his attorney, withdrew $4,000 from a joint account and converted $11,250 in cash to a coin-based product without disclosing it.After filing for divorce, Vernon deposited rental income into accounts solely owned or accessible by him and spent the funds without consulting Nichole or providing documentation for alleged expenses. He did not give her any of the rental income earned after the filing date.Why the court found dissipationUnder Indiana law, dissipation refers to the frivolous, unjustified spending of marital assets, including concealment and diversion of funds. The appellate court said the trial court’s findings met that standard.The court noted that Vernon attempted to conceal funds in a coin-based account, diverted $62,000 to an account Nichole could not access, and used $8,800 of marital assets for his own benefit. His accounting for rental income and expenses was described as questionable, and he consistently failed to produce accurate supporting documents.The trial court also found Vernon in contempt for willfully failing to pay mortgages, which created additional marital debt. That history of noncompliance strengthened the case for treating the property division as unequal.Why the 55 percent split was preservedNichole argued that an equal division of the marital estate would not be fair and equitable given the disparity in income between the spouses, the fact that the assets and debts were acquired because of the efforts of both spouses, and Vernon’s dissipation of marital assets. The trial court agreed.The court noted that Vernon had consistently made at least twice and possibly three times what Nichole made. The gap was large enough to warrant a move away from the assumed equal split even when her highest income was taken into account. The result was a 55 percent share of the marital estate for Nichole, with a cash payment of $138,219.45 from Vernon. The appellate court found that this outcome was supported by the evidence and did not constitute an abuse of discretion, as per the report.The rental income questionThe trial court also had to decide how much income the rental properties generated during the three years the divorce was pending. Nichole calculated a net value of $145,000, while Vernon claimed $0, despite earlier testimony suggesting a net profit of $10,000 to $20,000 per year.The court found it very difficult to determine the true net earnings because Vernon’s management of income and expenses was extensively commingled with personal finances. Multiple profit and loss spreadsheets he submitted showed different numbers for the same time period, and none offered documentation supporting the alleged expenses.After reviewing all the evidence, the trial court found that the net rental income over the three-year period was $60,000. The appellate court upheld that valuation as fair and reasonable, given the totality of the circumstances.What happens to the propertiesThe trial court ordered that the rental properties be listed for sale, with the proceeds divided equally after mortgage payments, closing costs and realtor fees. Vernon is responsible for paying the mortgages until each property is sold, but he can be reimbursed 50 percent of those payments from the sale proceeds.Any remaining balance owed to Nichole under the $138,219.45 settlement must be paid within 180 days after the rental properties are sold and proceeds distributed. The court also ordered that Vernon receive the marital residence on Woodlawn Avenue, on the condition that he removes Nichole’s name from the mortgage within 60 days.If Vernon is unable or unwilling to refinance the Woodlawn property within that window, the home must be listed for sale immediately. The court also ordered that the parties not create additional debt or encumbrances on any real estate while the properties are pending sale.Attorney’s fees and the broader lessonThe trial court ordered Vernon to reimburse Nichole $2,500 for attorney’s fees related to the contempt finding, and an additional $17,500 based on his higher earning potential and the complexity of the case. The appellate court upheld both amounts.The case is a reminder that in a divorce involving rental properties, financial transparency matters. When one spouse controls the accounts, the records and the rental platforms, the other spouse can be left with little visibility into what is happening.For the McIntoshes, the result was a 55 percent share of the marital estate for Nichole, a $138,219.45 payment, and a court order that the rental properties be sold with proceeds divided equally. articles.body: The judge who oversaw the first Lindsay Clancy murder trial has denied two more of her requests, including one to dismiss the three murder indictments against her. Massachusetts Superior Court Judge William Sullivan also denied Clancy’s motion to question the so-called holdout juror in the trial and examine court records related to the juror’s service. And he handed the prosecution a loss, rejecting its bid to prevent lawyers from freely discussing the case with the media. The issues were argued at a testy hearing last week, with another one on the books for next week — a date for the retrial could be set then. Clancy was charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her three young children. At her trial, her team didn’t deny that she killed the children before she attempted suicide, but it argued that she was in the throes of postpartum psychosis at the time. Following the mistrial, the Plymouth County District Attorney’s Office hasn’t announced whether it intends to proceed with retrying Clancy. articles.title: Hungarian police reportedly detain brother of ex-PM Viktor Orban
articles.summary: Aron Orban reportedly detained as Hungarian authorities raid properties linked to his business associates.
articles.body:
Former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban has accused the country’s new government of “political persecution” after the reported arrest of his younger brother.

Hungarian police arrested Aron Orban on Monday on suspicion of people smuggling, among other offences, according to a press report shared by Prime Minister Peter Magyar. Viktor Orban’s staunch opposition to immigration defined his 16 years in power that ended in defeat at elections in April.

News of the arrest was first reported by Kontroll, a news site owned by Magyar’s brother, Marton. Police carried out raids involving Aron Orban’s business associates but did not confirm whether he was among those detained, local media reported.

Viktor Orban accused the government of arresting his brother as a way to “divert attention” from other issues.

“I am the real target. My younger brother is simply being used to get to me,” he wrote on X.

Like other members of the Orban family, Aron built several successful businesses during his brother’s rule.

Last year, an investigation by news site Telex linked Aron Orban and his business associates to an alleged scheme involving visas for foreign guest workers.

Authorities said they had detained four people suspected of people smuggling.

Pro-EU conservative Magyar won a landslide election victory in April, ending 16 years of Orban’s rule, after promising to investigate his predecessor’s alleged corruption and abuse of power while in office.

articles.title: Booker Prize 2026: M John Harrison's 'baffling but brilliant' novel The End of Everything wins
articles.summary: M John Harrison becomes the oldest ever winner of the prestigious literary award at the age of 81.
articles.body:
Author M John Harrison has become the oldest ever winner of the Booker Prize, picking up the prestigious literary award for his post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything.

Harrison, 81, who has built a cult following over his 60-year career, was named the winner of the £50,000 prize at a ceremony in London on Monday.

The End of Everything is set in the years after a mysterious catastrophe that caused British society as we know it to collapse. It has divided opinion among readers, and was described as "bleak but brilliant" and "dreamlike and baffling" by one critic.

Dame Mary Beard, who chaired the Booker judges, said: "It's a challenging read, but some of the best fiction is challenging."

Dame Mary added: "It's a book that turns you upside down, raises a wry smile – and surprisingly, given the subject matter, leaves you with a twinge of optimism."

Harrison began writing in the 1960s and has published 13 novels, five short story collections and an "anti-memoir". He has now surpassed Margaret Atwood as the oldest ever Booker winner.

While he dislikes labels like science fiction and fantasy, he has been called "the titan of literary science fiction", and Booker Prize chief executive Gaby Wood said he is "the first Booker winner to have emerged from the bona fide SF world".

"He is a genuinely original thinker, a genre-defying writer who takes ideas seriously," Wood said.

"Though very unsettling, The End of Everything is not in fact a strange book. It's a realist book about a strange world, populated by desperate, unmoored characters."

The story follows a man and his aunt who must muddle through on the south-east English coast in the aftermath of an unexplained disaster and the arrival of mysterious alien beings.

The author has said he deliberately omitted as much explanation about the background to the events as possible, in order to make readers feel the same disorientation as the characters.

He has said: "The End of Everything is about trying to live as if nothing has gone wrong. It's a disaster story in which the disaster is the failure to comprehend."

He added: "I've passed on to the reader some of the puzzlement and confusion of the characters in the book as they face a future with the alien."

That approach has led to a mixed reaction. The Guardian praised the book but said "it won't be for everyone", while the New York Times said : "The more we learn about the conditions of this novel's broken world, the harder it is to grasp."

The Literary Review described it as "a work of uncanny beauty, tender and terrifying in equal parts", while the Telegraph said "you feel you're not so much reading as dreaming".

Another Telegraph critic wrote that it was "ultimately, in both skill and humour, a cut above" the other shortlisted books.

"And in an age when AI overlords keep threatening to kill us, and the Government has told us to stockpile tinned food and bottled water, it is, for once, a novel that you can genuinely call 'timely'."

The Booker Prize is an annual award for the best novel written in the English language and published in the year up to 30 September. It was launched in 1969.

This year's other shortlisted books were:

The Things We Never Say by Elizabeth Strout

When the shortlist was announced in September, Dame Mary said agreeing on the final six had been, "to put it mildly, hard work".

Another judge, US novelist Patricia Lockwood, said she had been "tossing books across the room" during judging sessions, while poet Raymond Antrobus described the selection as "a tussle".

The other judges were Pulp frontman Jarvis Cocker, and journalist, editor and critic Rebecca Liu.

Speaking about the final judging session, Dame Mary told reporters on Monday: "There was a lot of discussion, disagreement and debate. But nobody stomped off."

In a statement, she said the panel "spent a whole day debating the six remarkable novels on this year's shortlist" before reaching a unanimous decision to name Harrison the winner.

articles.title: Ahead of peace talks, Zelenskyy seeks PM Modi's help on ceasefire
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ahead of the Abu Dhabi peace talks, PM Narendra Modi and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke Monday with the latter briefing the PM
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ahead of the Abu Dhabi peace talks, PM Narendra Modi and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke Monday with the latter briefing the PM about latest developments related to the Russia-Ukraine conflict and Modi conveying India’s "firm commitment" to contributing in every possible way towards a peaceful resolution of the Russia-Ukraine war.The conversation took place a day before the trilateral peace dialogue involving Russia, Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi, and amid renewed Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. Ahead of the talks, where India's recent peace proposals are likely to be discussed too, India remained engaged with both sides on diplomatic initiatives as foreign minister S Jaishankar too spoke to his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov.Zelenskyy recalled Modi's latest peace message to President Vladimir Putin that it was time now to end the "endless war" and urged India to take more steps towards a ceasefire that can ensure food and energy security. Modi said in a post on X that he and Zelenskyy had a productive conversation – their first since they met on the margins of the G7 summit in France in June.Modi's message to Zelenskyy expressing India's readiness to facilitate peace is not new, but its timing is significant as this was the first time they spoke after Jaishankar revealed in early October India was actively mediating for establishment of safe corridors in the Black Sea for grain and energy exports."We reviewed our wide-ranging bilateral cooperation and agreed to further strengthen India-Ukraine ties. I thanked President Zelenskyy for sharing his perspectives on the ongoing conflict, its humanitarian aspects and various efforts to restore peace," said Modi in his own readout of the talks.Ukraine believes Russia has not responded positively to India's Black Sea shipping proposal and the call to end targeting of its energy sector. "The Prime Minister has said more than once, including directly to the Russian ‌leader, ⁠that now is the time to end the war, not to continue it," said Zelenskyy on X after his talks with Modi, urging India to identify steps it can take and also talks it can pursue with other leaders to bring the conflict to an end.“Food security could be one such area. We discussed Russia's blocking of grain exports via the Black Sea. India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors, and we are counting on these efforts to continue,” said the Ukrainian president.Zelenskyy also said Ukraine had always taken a constructive approach, and Russia must show the same readiness to de-escalate.“Russia must understand that the global economy and hundreds of millions of people around the world are suffering because of blocked sea routes. We agreed that our teams will stay in touch on these and other bilateral issues,” he said.An Indian readout said Modi reaffirmed India’s human-centric approach and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy.The 4th round of Russia-Ukraine peace talks mediated by the US are scheduled to begin in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. articles.title: Inflation likely took a breather last month as fuel prices fell
articles.summary: Tuesday’s CPI report will be the first snapshot of U.S. price growth since inflation-weary Americans voted for a Democratic sweep in the midterms.
articles.body:
Americans are tired of inflation, as last week's election results showed, but there may have been some relief last month as gasoline, diesel and jet fuel prices eased.

The consumer price index, which is scheduled for release at 8:30 a.m. ET on Tuesday, is expected to show an increase of 0.3% month-over-month, according to a survey of economists conducted by Bloomberg. Economists also project that so-called core inflation, which does not include food or energy prices, rose 0.2%.

In September, the CPI report showed prices grew 0.6% from August along with a 3.7% increase from a year earlier. (The October data will not include a year-ago number after the U.S. government shutdown disrupted the agency's data collection, forcing it to skip the October 2025 CPI report entirely.)

Even with some relief, the October data is set to illustrate the price pressures on consumers — a big factor in the Democrats' sweeping victories in the congressional midterm elections last week. Eighty-four percent of voters told NBC News' Exit Poll that they believed higher prices were a result of President Donald Trump's policies, and 39% said the economy was their No. 1 issue at the ballot box, according to the exit poll.

Those policies include global tariffs that add to the cost of products imported into the United States, as well as the war in Iran. Launched in February, that conflict has driven regular gas prices up 40%. Diesel fuel prices are 70% higher than at the start of the year.

That, in turn, pushed inflation higher across the U.S.. Economists have warned that the rise in this commercial fuel can quickly ripple across the economy. Diesel is a major input cost for the transportation industry that delivers goods, such as groceries, to store shelves around the world.

Gas prices declined last month, as Americans either voted early or geared up to cast their ballots on Election Day. On Oct. 1, the AAA national gas price average was $4.41 per gallon. At the end of the month, it was $4.18, a more than 5% drop.

As a result, Citigroup economists predicted that Tuesday's data will show "stabilizing and falling airfares, and limited pass through of higher energy costs into goods prices." They also said shelter inflation and services prices could also show some slowing.

Gas prices have continued trending downward in November, falling to $4 on Monday — although it's still significantly higher than before the Iran war.

Even as the oil price surge takes a breather, it may not last long. Throughout the Iran war, countries that are members of the International Energy Agency have released 400 million barrels of crude and related products , such as diesel, into the global market. "Restocking those inventories will create a floor under prices once the current conflict in the Middle East has faded," said Diane Swonk, chief economist at KPMG.

Given inflation's overall stubbornness, economists believe the Federal Reserve will remain on track to hike rates for the second time this year. The Fed's next two-day interest rate meeting will take place Dec. 8-9, right before the next inflation reading on Dec. 10.

Market odds for a December hike sat at 85% Monday afternoon.

"Still, details of Q4 data will be important for shifting inflation risks into 2027," Citi economists wrote.

Bank of America economists agreed, predicting that the report would be "a cooler start to fall," after multiple months of rising inflation.

Meanwhile, AI is also stoking inflation in other parts of the economy. In August, JPMorgan estimated that memory costs were on track to rise more than 400% from the end of 2024 through the end of 2026.

Tech companies are spending hundreds of billions of dollars on data centers and the equipment that fills those facilities, pushing memory prices higher. Those costs are being passed down to consumers. Consumer tech companies, including Apple , have raised their prices as a result.

articles.title: Motherwell feels like a 'failed project', say residents frustrated by closures
articles.summary: A council decision to demolish Motherwell Concert Hall is the latest in a long line of culture and leisure closures in the town.
articles.body:
A council decision to demolish Motherwell's well-used concert hall and replace it with a staff car park has left the town feeling like a "failed project from the 70s", residents have said.

The venue has been part of the town's cultural landscape for 50 years, but has been out of use since 2023 when potentially dangerous concrete was found.

The decision to knock it down last month follows the loss of swimming facilities and an ice rink in recent years, while the local town hall is being turned into flats.

North Lanarkshire Council said it continued to invest significantly across culture, leisure, housing and regeneration and its current projects were "a strong commitment to the town's future".

But local groups say the town is "overflowing" with houses, and called on the local authority to invest more in community facilities.

Matthew McCrossan worked at the Motherwell concert hall as a front of house staff member, having grown up watching shows on its stage.

"It was an accessible and affordable way of having culture in Motherwell," he said.

"If the building is unviable then the community should be consulted on what replaces it, not just deciding it will become 44 parking spaces."

The local authority insists the cost of fully repairing the B-listed theatre could be about £34m, a figure it cannot justify.

By contrast, turning it into a car park has an estimated price tag of £5.7m.

In Motherwell's heyday, thousands of people worked in the area, particularly at the Ravenscraig steelworks.

Its closure in 1992 devastated the wider region, and numerous other businesses and firms closed in the ensuing decades.

"Instead of drawing people to the town, everything being done is encouraging people to leave, and to focus on Motherwell as a transit area," says Bobby Miller, a retired science teacher involved with the Motherwell Deserves Better group.

"We are so focused on houses now. We are like a failed project from the 70s where these massive schemes are overflowing with houses, but there is absolutely nothing else."

A banner outside the town's Aquatec sports complex declares it to be "more than just a gym" - a tagline which raises eyebrows locally.

Both the swimming pool and ice rink which were previously part of the Aquatec have closed, meaning a large chunk of the building is no longer in use.

Earlier this year the whole building closed for several weeks due to issues with the heating during the winter.

Campaigner Luke Gilmour said he and others would be happy for such venues to be demolished if they were at risk of collapse - but they should be replaced with something else.

"It's depressing for the area for a start," he said. "There's an abundance of charity shops and vape shops, and nothing else.

"The gym, no-one is sure about the future of it - there are no plans to close the gym, but there are no plans to invest in it either."

North Lanarkshire Council disagrees with this assessment. It points to ongoing investment in heating and lighting facilities in the building.

But the campaigners say they consider that to be essential maintenance rather than investment.

Council investment has gone towards three new community hubs across North Lanarkshire, which will mix houses, shops and community facilities.

Council leader Jim Logue said: "While these projects take time to progress, they represent a strong commitment to the town's future."

The Ravenscraig hub may include a replacement for the Theatre and Concert Hall building, but nothing has been guaranteed.

Councillor Logue said that the concert hall demolition was the only option due to the cost of restoring the building, but "future cultural opportunities" will be explored in other spaces.

In the meantime, locals are advised to go to Airdrie's Town Hall, or use Motherwell's existing Heritage Centre, which has family events and exhibitions on.

But the concert hall hosted comedy, school shows, annual pantomimes and gigs by acts as varied as the Proclaimers, former Stone Roses singer Ian Brown and pop band UB40.

Jamie Keenan drummed with Motherwell rap-rock band the LaFontaines - a group which sold out Glasgow's Barrowlands, released several albums and toured at home and abroad.

They also played the concert hall several times.

"It's a blow because it's the only thing of its nature in the town," Keenan said.

"Some of the LaFontaines first gigs were there and just as it was shutting down I think it was almost becoming a B-type venue - getting acts who had played Glasgow earlier on a tour to come back and do Motherwell."

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

Matthew McCrossan is frustrated that a facility which was still putting on shows until the day it closed has been rendered a lost cause after three years of sitting derelict.

He and his brother Nick have protested to North Lanarkshire Council about the decision.

"I can sympathise with the council needing to save money, but it looks like they started with the decision to get the new car park, and then have worked backwards to substantiate this," he said.

"They could have spent money from their surplus, but that was used on the new community hubs instead."

The decision to demolish the concert hall has been backed by both Historic Environment Scotland (HES) and the Theatre Trust campaign group.

They agree the building has fallen into such disrepair demolition is the only option.

The Theatre Trust told BBC Scotland News it was working to ensure "theatre provision continues in the local area and to consider what longer-term plans could help achieve this."

However there remains scepticism about what this will involve. For those in the area, only sustained investment and a guarantee of new facilities will help.

"It's happened one thing at a time," said Gilmour.

"It's only when you start thinking about it you go 'they've shut everything down now, we have lost so much'."

The three-bedroom property is in lower Laurel Canyon, in an exclusive enclave at the base of Mount Olympus.Its exterior resembles a fairy-tale cottage among trees, while the interior features vivid colours and textures. The house spans 2,119 square feet and was built in 1926. According to Realtor, Wainwright bought the property in 2016 for $1.45 million and maintained its original features with personal touches. The home is set behind a gate and offers privacy, and is just minutes from Sunset Boulevard.What makes this 1926 Laurel Canyon house look like a fairy-tale cottageThe property is located in lower Laurel Canyon, at the base of Mount Olympus. The Spanish-style house, dating to 1926, occupies a gated parcel surrounded by trees. The tree-lined setting offers privacy, while Sunset Boulevard remains just minutes away. Listing agent Alexandre Anu of Douglas Elliman is marketing the home alongside Dag Eliason of Hilton & Hyland. According to Realtor, the gated property offers a high level of privacy while remaining just minutes from Sunset Boulevard. Its peaceful surroundings make it feel as though one has escaped the busy city of Los Angeles.The three-bedroom residence has 2,119 square feet of living space. Its exterior has the appearance of a fairy-tale cottage tucked among trees, while its interior brings together colourful finishes, textures and decor.Original features that Rufus Wainwright preserved in his homeWainwright purchased the 2,119-square-foot property in 2016 for $1.45 million. Since then, he has maintained its original features while adding personal touches. The period details include wood-beamed cathedral ceilings, stained-glass windows, built-in features, and custom millwork.Reportedly, Wainwright wanted to retain the home's original character while making it suitable for everyday living. The living room features pitched ceilings and a Batchelder fireplace. It also served as a place where the musician wrote a few songs. The room was described as having an inspirational and moody atmosphere.The house's combination of older details and Wainwright's creative choices gives its rooms a distinctive character, rather than the look of a modernised Spanish home.Colourful interiors and unusual features define Wainwright's storybook homeThe interior is described as a vibrant mix of colours, textures and decor. One property feature is an octagon-shaped library. The light-filled kitchen has custom cabinetry, marble countertops, built-in seating and a farmhouse sink. A Dutch door opens from the kitchen to the outdoor living area. The dining room has diamond-pane windows and was designed for entertaining. In the primary bedroom, sunlight reaches a space that looks out over the landscaped garden.The property offers a quiet escape for creative buyersThe primary bedroom opens onto a yard. The landscaped setting and surrounding trees add to the property's secluded feel. According to the Realtor, the home offers a peaceful retreat suited to activities such as writing or reading. The property has attracted interest from people in creative fields, including writers, artists, directors, and musicians. Its distinctive character and storybook-style atmosphere may appeal to buyers who appreciate its original charm rather than those seeking an updated Spanish-style home with modern features.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available property listing information and statements made by the listing agents.
