articles.title: In 2008, a Massachusetts couple bought oceanfront land to build a house, but neighbours repeatedly disrupted the construction; 18 years later, an appeals court upheld a $3.7 million verdict against them
articles.summary: In 2008, Margaret Reichenbach and her husband bought oceanfront land in Dartmouth, Massachusetts, with plans to build a new home.
articles.body: In 2008, Margaret Reichenbach and her husband bought oceanfront land in Dartmouth, Massachusetts, with plans to build a new home. But what should have been a straightforward construction project turned into an 18-year legal saga after neighbours repeatedly tried to stop or delay the work, interfered with contractors and allegedly trespassed on the property. On July 29, 2026, the Massachusetts Appeals Court upheld a jury verdict awarding the couple $3.7 million in damages and affirmed a permanent injunction against further interference, as per records on Findlaw.com.The case, Reichenbach v. Haydock, is a striking example of how far a property dispute can go when neighbours turn a boundary disagreement into a prolonged campaign of obstruction. The jury found that Timothy Haydock and Susan Moss violated the Massachusetts Civil Rights Act, committed trespass and intentionally interfered with the couple’s construction contract, conduct the appellate court said was supported by ample evidence. Read more details about it, as per the report, here:How the dispute beganThe Reichenbachs bought the oceanfront property in 2008 and began construction in 2009. They received a certificate of occupancy in 2014, but the home was not fully finished until 2016, years later than expected.The delay was not caused by weather, financing or ordinary construction problems. According to the court’s summary, the defendants engaged in a range of actions aimed at stymieing the project, including repeated petitions to the town’s conservation commission and the Department of Environmental Protection to stop or delay construction.When those efforts failed, the conduct escalated. The defendants interfered with the work of the couple’s surveyor, repeatedly harassed contractors, blocked workers’ vehicles, moved garbage cans close to the property line and trespassed on the land.What the jury heardThe case went to trial in Superior Court, where the jury spent 15 days hearing evidence. They took a view of the property and surrounding neighborhood, heard from 19 witnesses and reviewed 181 exhibits.The jury found the defendants liable on three counts: violation of the Massachusetts Civil Rights Act, trespass and intentional interference with contractual relations. The total damages award came to $3.7 million, with $1.5 million allocated to the civil rights claim, $200,000 to trespass and $2 million to interference with contract.After the verdict, the trial judge granted the Reichenbachs a permanent injunction preventing the defendants from interfering with their use and enjoyment of the property. The judge also denied the defendants’ requests for a stay of the injunction, a new trial and other post-judgment relief.Why the civil rights claim held upThe Massachusetts Civil Rights Act requires a plaintiff to show that someone interfered with their exercise or enjoyment of a constitutional or statutory right through threats, intimidation or coercion. The appellate court said the evidence easily met that standard.The court noted that Moss stood near the property boundary approximately 300 times during construction, often taking photographs of the activity. That behavior, combined with other actions aimed at interfering with the build, supported the inference that a reasonable person in the Reichenbachs’ position would have felt intimidated or put in fear.Haydock’s conduct was also found sufficient. The court cited a heated altercation with the couple’s general contractor on the property, forcing their painter off the road and yelling at him, and hiding in bushes near the property while staring at the Reichenbachs’ son, who has a disability.Why the trespass claim held upOn the trespass claim, the defendants argued there was no evidence they had entered the property without permission. The appellate court disagreed.A security guard testified to seeing Moss returning to her car from the direction of the property at night, which the court said allowed the jury to infer she had entered without permission. Haydock’s altercation with the general contractor on the property also supported the inference that he lacked permission, particularly since the defendants offered no affirmative evidence that the Reichenbachs had ever granted them access beyond easements.The court applied the standard legal definition of trespass, which requires entering or remaining on land in another’s possession without privilege. The evidence, viewed in the light most favorable to the plaintiffs, was enough for the jury to find that standard met.Why the contract interference claim held upThe defendants also argued that the Reichenbachs failed to prove a breach of contract, which they said was necessary for the interference claim. The appellate court rejected that argument, explaining that Massachusetts recognizes a form of interference with contract under Section 766A of the Restatement (Second) of Torts that does not require an actual breach.Instead, the plaintiff must show that the defendant intentionally and improperly interfered with performance of the contract, making it more expensive or burdensome. The court found that the defendants’ conduct did exactly that, increasing the cost of the construction project by at least $2 million.The jury heard evidence that the project’s cost ballooned from an initial estimate of roughly $4.2 million on the low end to a final cost of $10 million. The court said that evidence, along with testimony about the personal time and effort the Reichenbachs spent on meetings, appeals, counsel and consultants, was enough to support the $2 million award.Why the damages award survivedThe defendants argued that the damages were excessive and speculative. The appellate court disagreed, noting that $700,000 of the total was for emotional damages, which the court said are inherently difficult to prove with certainty but still compensable.The court also rejected the argument that the civil rights award duplicated the contract interference award. The jury was instructed not to duplicate damages, and the court presumed it followed that instruction. The $1 million in non-emotional distress damages under the civil rights claim was tied to the loss of use and enjoyment of the property, which the court said was fully accounted for by the evidence.On the contract interference award, the court said a reasonable approximation of compensatory damages is permissible in business tort cases where close measurement is impossible. The $2 million award was not markedly against the weight of the evidence, given the scale of the cost overruns and the burden the defendants’ conduct imposed.Why the injunction survivedThe defendants argued that the permanent injunction was unsupported by evidence and unconstitutionally vague. The appellate court rejected both arguments.The injunction prohibits the defendants from threatening, harassing, intimidating, photographing, coercing or surveilling the plaintiffs, their family members, employees, tenants, contractors, vendors and others lawfully on the property. It also bars conduct that an objectively reasonable person would conclude interferes with the plaintiffs’ use and enjoyment of the property.The court said the language was not vague because it used objective standards rather than subjective ones. It also said the injunction was not overbroad, since it was narrowly tailored to prevent the specific harms the jury found, including harassment of the Reichenbachs’ child and contractors.What the ruling meansThe appellate court affirmed the judgments in favor of the Reichenbachs on all three claims and upheld the permanent injunction. It also affirmed the denial of the defendants’ post-judgment motions.The plaintiffs are entitled to appellate attorney’s fees and costs under the Massachusetts Civil Rights Act. They have 14 days to submit a detailed request, and the defendants have 14 days after that to respond.The case shows how a neighbour dispute can escalate into a multi-million-dollar legal battle when conduct crosses the line from petitioning to harassment. For the Reichenbachs, the verdict and injunction represent a long-awaited end to a conflict that began with a piece of oceanfront land and a dream home.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Casal adota cinco irmãos e se emociona com gratidão dos filhos | G1
articles.standfirst: Joel Barros e Valéria Reis estão casados há treze anos e adotaram os cinco irmãos há sete meses. Irmãos viviam em um abrigo de Anápolis.
articles.summary: Joel Barros e Valéria Reis adotaram cinco irmãos que viviam em um abrigo de Anápolis. Sete meses depois, o pai conta como a chegada das crianças transformou a família.
articles.body:
O casal Joel Barros e Valéria Reis, que adotou cinco irmãos que viviam em um abrigo de Anápolis , a 55 km de Goiânia, contou que um dos momentos mais marcantes da adoção foi a chegada das crianças e dos adolescentes à casa onde passariam a morar. Ao g1 , Joel disse que se emocionou ao perceber a gratidão dos filhos por terem um lar e um espaço que poderiam chamar de seu.

“Eles são muito gratos por terem um lar, por terem quartos seus, onde podem dizer: 'Agora estou em casa, esses são os meus pais, essa é a minha família'. Eles diziam: 'Obrigado, papai. Obrigado, mamãe'. Isso rachava os nossos corações”, contou.

Casados há 13 anos, Joel e Valéria sonhavam em ter filhos havia alguns anos. O casal passou por exames e tratamentos, mas não conseguiu realizar o desejo de ter filhos biológicos. A princípio, os dois pensavam em adotar duas crianças. O que não imaginavam era que a família seria formada por cinco irmãos. Há sete meses, Rayane, de 14 anos, Laura, de 12, Yarin, de 10, Lucas, de 7, e Samuel, de 6, passaram a morar com eles.

Segundo Joel, as crianças também demonstravam o desejo de ter uma família. Quando souberam que seriam acolhidas pelo casal, o encontro foi marcado por lágrimas e abraços.

“Foi um dia que ficou marcado em nossos corações e também no coração deles. Um momento de muito choro e também de muita alegria de ambas as partes”, disse.

Joel Barros e Valéria Reis com os cinco irmãos que adotaram em Anápolis, Goiás — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Joel Barros

O primeiro contato do casal com o Instituto Cristão Evangélico (ICE), em Anápolis , aconteceu durante uma ação social da igreja que frequentavam. Algum tempo depois, Valéria conseguiu um emprego como mãe auxiliar na instituição e passou a acompanhar de perto a rotina das crianças acolhidas.

Nos fins de semana em que a esposa trabalhava, Joel também visitava o abrigo. Ele passava as tardes brincando com as crianças, jogando bola e tomando sorvete. Foi assim que se aproximou dos cinco irmãos.

“Eles me chamavam de tio. Era tio para lá, tio para cá, muitos abraços, era um grude”, relembrou.

Casal decidiu adotar os cinco irmãos de uma só vez

De acordo com Joel, que trabalha como representante comercial, a ideia inicial era adotar duas crianças. Mas os planos mudaram depois que ele e a esposa começaram a conviver com os irmãos.

“Eu particularmente sempre quis ter três filhos, porém o tempo não foi favorável para sermos pais biológicos. Fizemos vários exames e tratamentos e nunca veio um sinal de filhos”, contou.

A decisão de adotar os cinco irmãos foi acompanhada de oração, aproximação e cumprimento das etapas legais. Segundo Joel, o casal passou por todas as fases exigidas no processo, desde a entrega dos documentos até os encontros e as entrevistas com psicólogos, assistentes sociais e profissionais da Justiça.

“Começamos a conhecer como era o processo de adoção e entregamos todos os documentos exigidos. Participamos de muitos encontros e entrevistas com psicólogos, assistentes sociais e profissionais da Justiça. Passamos por todas as etapas, sem pular nenhuma. Isso é importante demais”, contou.

Joel Barros compartilha momentos de carinho com os filhos após adoção de cinco irmãos em Anápolis — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Joel Barros

Chegada dos cinco filhos mudou a rotina da família

A chegada de cinco filhos de uma só vez exigiu mudanças na rotina. Joel e Valéria precisaram trocar de carro, reorganizar a vida escolar das crianças e aprender a lidar com as particularidades de cada uma.

O período de aproximação também teve desafios. Segundo o pai, alguns dos irmãos passaram a apresentar comportamentos mais infantis, enquanto o casal buscava entender as necessidades e o jeito de cada filho.

Mesmo com as dificuldades, Joel conta que a convivência se tornou cada vez mais próxima. Hoje, os sete dividem uma rotina de estudos, brincadeiras, música e momentos em família.

As três filhas mais velhas gostam de tocar instrumentos e participam de um projeto musical e da orquestra da igreja que frequentam.

Valéria Reis com os cinco filhos adotivos; irmãos estão há sete meses com a família — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Joel Barros

Sete meses depois, casal fala sobre a experiência da adoção

Sete meses após a chegada dos irmãos, Joel diz que a sensação é de que eles sempre fizeram parte da família. Segundo ele, a convivência tem momentos difíceis, como acontece em qualquer casa, mas também é cheia de descobertas.

Para o pai, a experiência mostrou que a decisão de adotar envolve muito mais do que condições materiais, embora reconheça os desafios de criar cinco filhos.

“Não precisa de riqueza para fazer a diferença. Tem muitas crianças que estão em um orfanato, e o que elas mais querem é apenas um pai ou uma mãe que deem amor, afeto, carinho e um lar”, afirmou.

Joel diz que a família ainda está aprendendo a viver essa nova fase. Entre mudanças de rotina, responsabilidades e momentos de carinho, ele e Valéria passaram de um casal que sonhava em ter filhos a pais de cinco irmãos.

“Essa é a maior riqueza que existe, chama-se família”, concluiu.

Valéria Reis e os cinco irmãos durante comemoração em família; casal decidiu adotar todas as crianças para mantê-las juntas — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Joel Barros

Adoção dos cinco irmãos emociona internautas

A adoção dos cinco irmãos por Joel e Valéria também chamou a atenção nas redes sociais. Entre os comentários, internautas elogiaram a decisão do casal de manter as crianças juntas e destacaram a importância de os irmãos crescerem na mesma família. A história também recebeu mensagens de pessoas que conhecem os novos pais.

“Que história linda! Adotar já é um ato de amor gigante, mas não separar os cinco irmãos e acolhê-los a todos é verdadeiramente divino”, escreveu uma internauta. Outra pessoa comentou: “O tipo de notícia que vale a pena abrir o celular”.

A repercussão também trouxe relatos de quem conhece Valéria. Uma ex-aluna contou que ficou feliz ao descobrir que a antiga professora havia adotado os irmãos. “Valéria foi uma ótima professora do meu ensino médio. Quando eu vi, fiquei feliz demais por ela”, escreveu.

Outros internautas destacaram o desejo antigo do casal de ter filhos e a chegada dos cinco irmãos de uma só vez. “Sonho era grande, veio logo 5” , brincou uma pessoa. “Só Deus sabe o quanto essas crianças foram desejadas no coração desses pais”, comentou outra.

A história ainda despertou reações de pessoas que acompanham a trajetória do casal. “Sempre que vejo essa notícia, meu coração se alegra. Só quem conhece esse casal sabe que são pessoas amáveis”, afirmou uma internauta.

articles.title: Como elo entre Trump e CEO da Nvidia coincidiu com decisões favoráveis | G1
articles.standfirst: Jensen Huang se relacionou com mulher apontada como agente da inteligência chinesa. CEO da Nvidia é aliado do presidente americano e participa de eventos frequentes na Casa Branca.
articles.summary: Jensen Huang se relacionou com mulher apontada como agente da inteligência chinesa. CEO da Nvidia é aliado do presidente americano e participa de eventos frequentes na Casa Branca.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , e o CEO da Nvidia , Jensen Huang , desenvolveram uma relação próxima desde o início do atual mandato do republicano. Um dos aliados mais próximos de Trump no Vale do Silício, o executivo se tornou presença frequente na Casa Branca e participou de encontros importantes entre o governo americano e a China .

▶️ Contexto: A Nvidia está no centro de um escândalo após a imprensa americana revelar que o CEO da empresa teve um relacionamento com uma mulher apontada por autoridades dos Estados Unidos como agente da inteligência chinesa.

Segundo uma reportagem do jornal The New York Times, Huang teve um relacionamento com Alice Huang, ex-executiva da Megaspeed, empresa de data centers sediada em Singapura.

Apesar do sobrenome em comum, os dois não têm parentesco.

Autoridades americanas investigaram Alice e concluíram que ela atuava como agente da inteligência chinesa.

Segundo o NYT, a Megaspeed comprou mais de US$ 4,8 bilhões em chips da Nvidia nos últimos dois anos.

A empresa onde Alice trabalhava também foi investigada por autoridades dos Estados Unidos, sob suspeita de ter ajudado Pequim a obter acesso a chips avançados de inteligência artificial cuja exportação para a China é proibida.

O relacionamento de Huang e aproximação dele com Trump coincidiu com uma série de decisões da Casa Branca favoráveis à fabricante de chips. A Nvidia ocupa posição central na disputa tecnológica entre Estados Unidos e China.

A empresa é uma das maiores fabricantes de semicondutores do mundo e produz componentes fundamentais para o desenvolvimento de inteligência artificial.

Os chips da Nvidia são usados para treinar e operar modelos da tecnologia e alimentam muitos dos centros de dados de grandes empresas.

Esses componentes também estão no centro de uma disputa entre os Estados Unidos e a China. Desde 2022, o governo norte-americano mantêm controles de exportação para limitar o acesso chinês aos chips mais avançados da Nvidia e aos equipamentos necessários para produzi-los.

A estratégia dos Estados Unidos era preservar a vantagem americana na corrida tecnológica.

Mais recentemente, no entanto, Trump passou a defender uma abordagem mais flexível. O presidente argumentou que as restrições poderiam prejudicar as próprias empresas americanas e abriu espaço para que a Nvidia ampliasse as vendas de componentes à China.

Veja os principais episódios da aproximação entre Trump e Huang:

Abril de 2025: Huang participou de um jantar no clube Mar-a-Lago, de Trump, na Flórida. Naquele mês, o governo americano recuou dos planos de restringir a venda de determinados chips da Nvidia para a China.

Dezembro de 2025: Trump autorizou a venda de chips mais avançados da Nvidia para clientes aprovados na China, mediante uma cobrança de 25% sobre as operações.

Maio de 2026: Huang viajou com Trump à China a bordo do Air Force One. Foi a primeira visita de um presidente americano ao país em quase uma década.

Setembro de 2026: O CEO da Nvidia participou do jantar de Estado oferecido por Trump ao presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, na Casa Branca.

Outubro de 2026: Trump concedeu a Huang a Medalha Nacional de Ciência, a mais alta honraria científica dos Estados Unidos.

Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, ao lado de Donald Trump, presidente dos Estados Unidos, em foto de 8 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Reuters/Evan Vucci

A proximidade entre os dois ganhou uma dimensão ainda mais delicada depois que o jornal The New York Times revelou que Trump havia sido informado sobre suspeitas envolvendo o CEO da Nvidia cerca de um ano antes.

De acordo com o New York Times, integrantes do governo Trump temiam que uma reação às suspeitas prejudicasse os negócios da Nvidia e complicasse as relações entre os Estados Unidos e China.

Por isso, segundo a imprensa americana, o presidente não tomou nenhuma medida após ser informado sobre o caso.

Em outra reportagem, publicada neste domingo (8), o jornal afirmou que o secretário de Estado norte-americano, Marco Rubio, supervisionou um memorando altamente confidencial que alertava autoridades de alto escalão do governo sobre o relacionamento de Huang.

Questionado sobre o assunto na segunda-feira (9), Trump afirmou que o FBI está investigando o caso.

Um dia antes, Trump afirmou que considera o CEO da Nvidia "uma boa pessoa". Sobre as acusações, o presidente afirmou que Huang "provavelmente tem uma explicação" e que é necessário ouvi-lo.

articles.title: Mulher que morreu em voo para RO voltava para casa após visitar irmã | G1
articles.standfirst: Nair Carrier Dinis, de 76 anos, era natural do Paraná, mas morava em Rondônia há vários anos. Corpo será trasladado para Ariquemes, onde será sepultado.
articles.summary: Mulher morre em voo para Porto Velho após visitar a irmã: Nair Dinis, de 76 anos, passou mal na decolagem e será sepultada em Ariquemes nesta terça-feira.
articles.body:
O corpo de Nair Carrier Dinis, de 76 anos, que morreu após passar mal durante um voo com destino a Porto Velho, deve ser levado para Rondônia nesta terça-feira (10). O sepultamento será realizado em Ariquemes (RO), onde ela morava.

Uma familiar contou ao g1 que Nair era natural do Paraná, mas se mudou para Rondônia depois de se casar. Ela construiu a vida no estado e, segundo a ex-nora, não conseguiu mais se adaptar ao clima do Paraná quando voltou para visitar parentes.

A viagem tinha justamente o objetivo de passar um período com uma irmã que mora no estado. Nair estava retornando para casa quando passou mal durante o voo.

"Ela tinha ido ficar um tempo com a irmã dela. O irmão dela infelizmente, no início do ano faleceu, e ela só tinha uma irmã lá. Ela foi pra ficar um pouco com essa irmã dela e estava voltando pra casa", contou a familiar.

A ex-nora relatou ainda que Nair já enfrentava problemas de saúde. A idosa tinha familiares em Ariquemes, entre eles uma neta e uma bisneta, que moravam com ela.

Informações obtidas pelo g1 apontam que os procedimentos burocráticos para a liberação e o traslado do corpo ainda estavam sendo resolvidos em Brasília. Depois da chegada a Rondônia, o corpo será levado para Ariquemes.

Nair Carrier Dinis, de 76 anos, que morreu após passar mal durante um voo — Foto: Reprodução/acervo pessoal

De acordo com a plataforma FlightAware, o voo LA 3600 decolou de Brasília às 21h30 e chegou a sobrevoar a região em círculos por cerca de 40 minutos, antes de retornar e pousar no aeroporto de origem.

Testemunhas que estavam no mesmo voo contaram ao g1 que a passageira começou a passar mal logo após a decolagem.

A companhia aérea informou que Nair foi atendida voluntariamente por um médico que estava a bordo. Outra passageira, que é enfermeira e ajudou no atendimento, contou ao g1 que a vítima começou a apresentar sangramento pela boca durante o voo

Em nota, a Latam Airlines Brasil lamentou profundamente o falecimento da passageira e prestou solidariedade aos familiares e amigos. A companhia também disse que está prestando todo o suporte necessário à família neste momento.

Como o avião precisou retornar ao aeroporto, os demais passageiros foram reacomodados em outro voo, que decolou de Brasília às 3h08 e pousou em Porto Velho às 4h39 desta segunda-feira (09).

articles.title: Estudante da Bahia que morreu no Enem era cardiopata desde bebê | G1
articles.standfirst: Família acredita que a tensão do exame contribuiu para mal-estar. Menina passou mal e desmaiou no banheiro da escola onde a prova era aplicada. Ela fazia ensino médio na mesma unidade.
articles.summary: Família acredita que a tensão do exame contribuiu para mal-estar. Menina passou mal e desmaiou no banheiro da escola onde a prova era aplicada
articles.body:
A estudante de 16 anos que morreu após passar mal durante a realização do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) , em Cansanção , no norte da Bahia, era cardiopata desde bebê e fazia a prova pela primeira vez. A informação foi divulgada ao g1 pela família da adolescente na segunda-feira (9).

Iza Lara dos Santos Oliveira morreu no domingo (8), primeiro dia do exame. Os familiares dela acreditam que a tensão da prova contribuiu para o mal-estar. A menina desmaiou após pedir para ir ao banheiro da escola onde o Enem era aplicado.

A situação aconteceu no Colégio Estadual de Tempo Integral (CETI) Senhor do Bonfim, mesma instituição onde a adolescente fazia o ensino médio. A família diz que foi o pai da garota que foi acionado após o desmaio e dirigiu com ela até o hospital.

"Ela foi encontrada desmaiada no chão do banheiro. Começaram a a ligar para o meu pai para ir buscar. Ou seja, em nenhum momento houve ambulância, Samu [Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência] ou qualquer outra coisa. O que aconteceu foi meu pai encontrando a filha dele jogada no chão do banheiro", disse Yuri dos Santos, irmão de Iza Lara.

O jovem pontuou ainda que, já na unidade de saúde, a adolescente passou por diversas tentativas de reanimação, sem sucesso, e, ao ser intubada, o óbito foi constatado. "Assim que tentou, ela foi a óbito", contou.

Segundo informou o Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep) em nota divulgada ainda no domingo, a adolescente relatou um mal-estar durante a aplicação da prova, recebeu assistência médica e foi encaminhada para uma unidade de saúde, mas não resistiu.

No posicionamento, o órgão não detalha quem levou a menina para o hospital. O g1 solicitou posicionamento sobre o assunto, mas não tinha recebido retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

O irmão da estudante contou que a primeira cirurgia de Iza Lara aconteceu quando ela ainda tinha oito dias de vida, após uma primeira parada cardíaca.

Na ocasião, a família descobriu que a menina tinha sopro cardíaco — um ruído produzido pelo fluxo de sangue quando passa pelas estruturas do coração.

🔎 O barulho, ouvido pelos médicos durante consulta, é um sintoma provocado pelo crescimento exagerado e fraqueza do coração.

Ao longo da vida, a garota ainda passou por outros três procedimentos e usava um marca-passo. Segundo Yuri dos Santos, a família se organizava para mais uma cirurgia ainda nesse ano, mas a irmã estava bem. Ela se inscreveu para o Enem para se preparar para fazer novamente quando encerrasse o ensino médio.

"Eu acredito que foi muita pressão que ela vivenciou no período da prova. Estava muito quente também, e, como era a primeira prova dela do ENEM, eu acho que ela ficou muito ansiosa, e aí começou a passar mal, na sala de aula", destacou.

O corpo da adolescente foi sepultado nesta segunda-feira, em Cansanção, onde a família mora.

Tanto o Inep quanto a Prefeitura de Cansanção lamentaram a morte da adolescente e se solidarizaram com familiares e amigos dela, em nota. No texto da administração municipal, é destaca a comoção causada pela perda da jovem.

O colégio, que é administrado pela Secretaria Estadual de Educação, também emitiu nota de pesar e suspendeu as aulas na segunda-feira , em respeito à memória de Iza Lara. O funcionamento só será retomado nesta terça (10).

articles.title: 'Parecia que ia terminar o mundo', diz morador sobre tornado no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Fenômeno atingiu Palmeira das Missões e Santo Augusto no último sábado (7). Cenário nas áreas mais afetadas é de limpeza, retirada de destroços e reconstrução.
articles.summary: Fenômeno atingiu Palmeira das Missões e Santo Augusto no último sábado (7). Cenário nas áreas mais afetadas é de limpeza, retirada de destroços e reconstrução.
articles.body:
Três dias após a passagem do tornado que atingiu cidades do Norte do Rio Grande do Sul , moradores tentam reconstruir casas, empresas e propriedades arrasadas pela força dos ventos.

Em Palmeira das Missões , quem viveu a madrugada do último sábado (7) ainda se recupera do susto:

"Ali começou aquele barulhão, parecia que ia terminar o mundo. (...) Foi desesperador", relata o servidor público Natálio Antunes.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, o tornado deixou um rastro de destruição de cerca de três quilômetros em linha reta no município , desde o Bairro Félix até a Linha Capão Alto. Viveiros, residências e empresas ficaram destruídos pelo caminho.

Empresa do ramo agrícola atingida por tornado em Palmeira das Missões — Foto: Reprodução/ RBS TV

Enquanto os prejuízos ainda são contabilizados, o cenário nas áreas mais afetadas é de limpeza, retirada de destroços e reconstrução .

Além de ver anos de trabalho destruídos em poucos minutos, o empreendedor Gelson Cenci conta que também ajudou a socorrer um colega de trabalho que foi carregado pelos ventos. O homem foi encontrado desacordado em uma área de mata.

"Fui procurar ele. Ele tava dentro do mato, desmaiado. Acordou a hora que eu cheguei. Aí socorri ele e levei pro hospital", recorda.

De acordo com Gelson, a casa onde o colega estava foi completamente destruída:

O trabalhador, de 38 anos, recebeu alta hospitalar.

Em Santo Augusto, no Noroeste do Rio Grande do Sul, a cerca de 60 quilômetros de Palmeira das Missões, os moradores também convivem com os efeitos de um outro tornado .

A prefeitura decretou situação de emergência após a passagem do fenômeno. Cerca de 480 pessoas foram afetadas e 120 residências sofreram danos, segundo levantamento da Defesa Civil.

Outros 12 moradores precisaram deixar as residências e foram abrigados em casas de parentes ou incluídos no programa de aluguel social.

Casas destelhadas e um ferido no RS; passagem de tornado é investigada — Foto: Defesa Civil de Santo Augusto

A aposentada Anilda Vergor não sabe onde foi parar o telhado que foi arrancado da residência onde mora.

"Não sei até onde foi o telhado, até agora. (...) Ninguém sabe. Foi questão de minutos. Não deu tempo nem de respirar", conta.

A força dos ventos arrancou árvores, derrubou postes e danificou a rede elétrica.

A prefeita Lilian Fontoura Depiere afirma que o foco atual são ações de limpeza e auxílio às famílias.

"Estamos trabalhando para o restabelecimento da cidade, limpeza, ajuda às pessoas nas suas casas. E a gente fala para a comunidade que quem precisar, que a gente ainda não conseguiu chegar em todo mundo, que pode nos procurar na Assistência Social", diz a prefeita.

articles.title: Como banco digital que quebrou no Paraguai chegou a concentrar contas de 6 em cada 10 adultos do país | G1
articles.standfirst: Instituição tinha quase 3 milhões de clientes e era popular entre os jovens pela pouca burocracia para abrir contas; paralisação deixou milhões de pessoas sem acesso ao dinheiro.
articles.summary: Instituição tinha quase 3 milhões de clientes e era popular entre os jovens pela pouca burocracia para abrir contas; paralisação deixou milhões de pessoas sem acesso ao dinheiro.
articles.body:
O Ueno, banco digital que foi declarado insolvente em 3 de novembro, chegou a quase 3 milhões de clientes no Paraguai, o equivalente a cerca de seis em cada dez adultos do país. A instituição era especialmente popular entre os jovens, atraídos pela facilidade para abrir uma conta e pela pouca documentação exigida.

A paralisação do banco deixou milhões de pessoas sem acesso ao dinheiro que mantinham nas contas. Entre elas, estavam estudantes, comerciantes e trabalhadores que dependiam dos serviços da instituição para as despesas do dia a dia.

Uma estudante brasileira de medicina que vive no Paraguai contou ao Fantástico que a maioria dos colegas de faculdade também tinha conta no Ueno. Segundo ela, a instituição chamava a atenção dos jovens por exigir menos documentos do que outros bancos.

Protestos no Paraguai após crise do Ueno Bank. — Foto: Reprodução / Fantástico

"Era um banco que não pedia tanta documentação como os outros, então isso chamou muito a atenção dos jovens", afirmou.

A facilidade para abrir uma conta também foi um dos fatores que fizeram o banco se tornar conhecido entre brasileiros que vivem no país.

Com a paralisação, os efeitos chegaram à rotina dos estudantes. Uma das brasileiras entrevistadas contou que faltou à faculdade porque não tinha dinheiro para pagar a corrida de carro por aplicativo.

Outra cliente relatou a surpresa ao tentar acessar o aplicativo depois de saber da notícia.

"Eu vi a notícia, mas eu fiquei: 'Não, deve ser brincadeira'. Entrei no aplicativo, não abriu, e eu falei: 'Parece que não é brincadeira'", contou.

Brasileiros com conta no Ueno Bank do Paraguai aguardam para receberem dinheiro de volta. — Foto: Reprodução / Fantástico

A dimensão do Ueno ajuda a explicar o alcance da crise. Com quase 3 milhões de clientes, o banco atendia o equivalente a cerca de seis em cada dez adultos paraguaios.

Na terça-feira (3), a instituição foi declarada insolvente. Isso significa que não tinha mais capacidade financeira mínima para continuar operando. Na ocasião, dispunha de menos da metade do valor exigido por lei para manter suas atividades.

O banco também movimentava o equivalente a US$ 800 milhões de órgãos ligados ao Estado paraguaio. Parte dos recursos vinha da saúde e da Previdência Social.

A crise atingiu ainda brasileiros que mantinham dinheiro na instituição. Um comerciante ouvido pelo Fantástico disse que parte do capital de sua empresa ficou retida, dificultando o pagamento de fornecedores e funcionários e a compra de novas mercadorias.

O Fundo de Garantia de Depósitos do Paraguai informou que os clientes serão divididos em grupos para receber o dinheiro gradualmente. A garantia cobre cerca de US$ 29 mil por pessoa. Valores acima desse limite não têm recuperação assegurada.

articles.title: Fábrica operante vai a leilão com lance inicial de R$ 48 milhões no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Ditália Imóveis, de Monte Belo do Sul, teve falência decretada após credores rejeitarem plano de recuperação. Complexo industrial opera com cerca de 120 funcionários.
articles.summary: Ditália Imóveis, de Monte Belo do Sul, teve falência decretada após credores rejeitarem plano de recuperação. Complexo industrial opera com cerca de 120 funcionários.
articles.body:
Fábrica da Datália Imóveis, em Monte Belo do Sul — Foto: Ditália/Divulgação

Uma fábrica de móveis localizada em Monte Belo do Sul , cidade de 2,5 mil habitantes na Serra Gaúcha, vai a leilão nesta terça-feira (9). A empresa Ditália Imóveis teve a falência decretada após os credores rejeitarem o plano de recuperação judicial.

Por determinação da Justiça, o complexo industrial continua em operação com aproximadamente 120 colaboradores diretos e e-commerce. A linha de produção inclui sofás, tábuas de passar roupa, móveis auxiliares e móveis planejados.

O lance inicial é de R$ 48 milhões , mas os ativos do empreendimento são avaliados em R$ 83 milhões e o pagamento pode ser realizado em até 72 parcelas. A competição está limitada a 16 concorrentes que participaram da primeira fase do leilão — não há mais como participar desta etapa, afirma o leiloeiro.

O diferencial, neste caso, é de que a Ditália Imóveis segue em pleno funcionamento. A Justiça determinou um administrador judicial e a empresa segue operando .

"Não é toda empresa que tem suas portas fechadas que o Judiciário permite que ela prossiga, para não perder o seu valor intrínseco, que é a operação. Foi um despacho no sentido de ter uma falência com a continuidade das operações", afirma o leiloeiro Norton Fernandes.

Atualmente, a fábrica é gerida por um administrador judicial nomeado pela Justiça, que controla o fluxo de caixa, os materiais e as operações diárias.

"O administrador judicial, que normalmente é escolhido pelo juiz, é uma pessoa de confiança do juízo que detém expertise para poder controlar isso tudo", explica Fernandes.

O complexo industrial tem área total dos terrenos de 136.650 metros quadrados, com cerca de 40 mil metros quadrados de área construída.

O leilão abrange os imóveis, os estoques de matérias-primas e produtos acabados, além de um parque de bens móveis composto por 1.908 itens, incluindo máquinas, equipamentos de informática e veículos, avaliados em mais de R$ 29 milhões.

O g1 tentou contato com o administrador judicial, e até a publicação desta reportagem não houve retorno.

articles.title: The superpower battle over energy, and the impact on your bills
articles.summary: A tug-of-war between China and the US could have a big impact on energy costs, but who will win?
articles.body:
A gas rig in the North Sea. An oil field in Texas. A solar panel factory in China. They can feel a world away, but your energy bill says otherwise.

In January, it could jump by more than a quarter – around £460 extra a year for the typical UK household – according to the latest forecasts from the big suppliers British Gas, EDF and E.ON.

For the second time in four years, a war thousands of miles away is landing in British inboxes.

Since US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, oil and gas prices have soared.

Winter is expected to push them higher still: demand for gas is rising just as Europe's winter gas stores are at their lowest since records began in 2011.

And there's a bigger threat looming over all of this: the warming climate. Cutting carbon emissions is essential to limit future warming and avoid the most damaging effects of climate change. But keeping bills down while cutting emissions is proving hard – and not just for the UK.

As world leaders gather this week in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the UN climate summit, the same tension is playing out around the world. Energy and climate policy has become the front line in a contest between the world's two energy superpowers, leaving everyone else squeezed in between.

America is betting on fossil-fuel molecules: pumping record volumes of oil and gas and pressing its allies to buy them. China is betting on electrons: flooding the world with the solar panels, batteries and electric cars that can replace those fuels.

Whether the bet on fossil fuels or renewables wins will shape not just what the world pays for energy, but how fast it can cut the emissions that are heating the planet.

The UK, which already buys nearly a quarter of its imported gas from America and much of its clean energy kit from China, is being pulled both ways. So which path will it take? Is there a middle way and what will it all mean for your bills?

On the Moray Firth near Inverness, a long spit of sand and dunes curls out into the sea at Whiteness Head. Behind it lies a yard where, for nearly 30 years, thousands of workers built the giant platforms that opened up North Sea oil.

Ming Yang, one of China's biggest wind turbine makers, wanted to bring it back to life with a £1.5bn factory and up to 1,500 jobs initially generated. In March, after US lawmakers had urged the UK to block it, ministers did just that, citing national security.

Last month, they approved a new North Sea gas field, Jackdaw. No to Chinese wind turbines; yes to North Sea gas.

Few countries are more exposed to the energy shock than the UK. Gas heats most homes and, much of the time, sets the wholesale price of electricity. The last shock, after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, cost households an extra £63bn – around £2,200 each – according to the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit and E3G, two climate and energy research organisations.

Less than half of the UK's gas now comes from its own North Sea fields, and the energy we import often comes from places that turn out to be unstable or unreliable.

At the same time, Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh says tackling climate change remains a priority after Britain's hottest summer on record. The heatwaves, droughts and wildfires it brought would have been almost impossible without global warming, the Met Office's chief scientist told BBC Panorama.

But when I pressed Fahnbulleh on which matters most, bills or climate, she was unequivocal: "With the cost of living biting, affordability is my overriding objective, without a doubt."

"We are far too exposed to global markets we have no control over," Fahnbulleh told me. "What's the solution to that? Homegrown clean energy."

There are two ways to make Britain's energy more homegrown: drill for more of it, or build more of it.

Within hours of Jackdaw's approval, US President Donald Trump - at war with wind turbines since objecting to a wind farm near his Aberdeenshire golf course in 2006 - took to Truth Social. "They should go FULL BLAST!!!" he wrote. "TAKE DOWN THE COSTLY AND RIDICULOUS WINDMILLS!"

Now the UK government faces a tougher choice - whether to approve Rosebank, west of Shetland, the UK's largest undeveloped oil field.

Rosebank is far bigger than Jackdaw - Fahnbulleh has said it would produce about seven times the emissions - and it is mostly oil, not gas. The subject has reportedly split the cabinet. A decision is expected within weeks.

The government's opponents are already blaming high bills on its reluctance to drill. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has told the prime minister to "stop faffing about" and give permission, calling drilling "the only way we can protect families from rising bills".

"If we use our own gas… that will bring our bills down," says Reform UK's Richard Tice.

Last week's US midterms were a reminder of the political risks. Soaring petrol prices are widely seen as a key reason Trump's Republicans lost control of Congress.

But when I asked Fahnbulleh whether producing more British oil and gas would bring bills down, she was clear. "No, it doesn't," she said. "In the end, the oil and gas is sold on global markets."

Critics go further. Rosebank "doesn't really do anything for energy security", argues Tessa Khan of the campaign group Uplift, which has fought the field in the courts. "What it does do is send a very dangerous signal about the UK's seriousness about addressing climate change after the summer that we've just had."

Zoom out, though, and the row looks rather different. The North Sea is in long-term decline. Output has fallen by more than two-thirds since its peak in 1999, and the Office for Budget Responsibility expects it to keep falling by around 10% a year – even with Rosebank, which its forecast assumes goes ahead.

Whatever ministers decide, the basin's most productive days are behind it. Jackdaw's reserves amount to only a few months of UK gas demand, while Rosebank contains less than a year's worth of our oil consumption.

And last week the government introduced a bill to write its ban on new exploration licences into law. Rosebank, which is already licensed, is not covered. That could let ministers have it both ways: approve the last big field, while promising there will never be another.

With bills set to rise again in January, that may prove a tempting combination.

Gas is bought, burned and bought again. A wind turbine or solar panel costs money to put up but can then generate electricity for decades without needing shipments of fuel.

The government's climate advisers, the Climate Change Committee, calculate that a future price shock like 2022's would push household energy bills up 59% if Britain stayed on a high-carbon path - but only 4% if it focused on renewables.

The cost of power from new solar farms fell by 90% between 2010 and 2024, and from onshore wind by 70%, according to the International Renewable Energy Agency. But the recent bout of global inflation has been pushing initial costs back up. Last year the Danish developer Ørsted scrapped plans for Hornsea 4, a giant wind farm off the Yorkshire coast, blaming soaring supply chain costs.

Higher interest rates have made things worse. Most of the cost of a wind or solar farm comes up front, so developers must borrow heavily before they generate any power.

And there is another problem. Britain needs expensive new electricity networks to bring that renewable power to the towns and cities where it is needed. Meanwhile, gas-fired stations still frequently set wholesale power prices - meaning any cost savings are not always reflected in customer bills.

All of which means building more renewables does not automatically mean lower household bills.

And there is another issue - China's dominance of clean tech. It makes the vast majority of the world's solar panels and batteries, and around two-thirds of its electric cars.

And China's lead is growing. In March, its exports of solar panels, batteries and electric cars hit a record, up 70% on a year earlier, according to the think tank Ember.

The UK wants to escape the fossil fuels that leave households exposed to price shocks and keep adding to global warming. Much of the technology needed to replace those fuels comes from China - a country it is increasingly reluctant to depend on.

I asked Fahnbulleh whether Britain was swapping dependence on petrostates for dependence on Beijing. "Well, look, we are," she said, adding: "we've got a diversified global market".

Britain will keep buying from China where it needs to, says Fahnbulleh, but she wants more of the kit made here. "I want to see turbines," she said.

Yet UK-built turbines were exactly what Ming Yang was offering.

"There was a security risk, and national security comes first and foremost," says Fahnbulleh. The government has never publicly explained what that risk was.

Two days before Jackdaw was approved, Japan's Sumitomo Electric opened Britain's first HVDC subsea cable factory at Nigg, a short way up the coast from Whiteness Head, creating up to 250 jobs.

Foreign investment, then - just not from China.

Earlier this year the US formally left the Paris climate agreement and is not expected to send a delegation to this year's COP. Without American pressure, others have less reason to make bold promises: national pledges now add up to a cut in global emissions of just 6% by 2035, the UN says – a tenth of what scientists say is needed to limit warming to 1.5C.

China is beginning to fill the space. Li Shuo, of the Asia Society Policy Institute, calls it a "role reversal". Once "a very conservative player" at climate talks, China now sees pushing the global climate agenda as serving its national interest – and, he says, "we're only at the beginning of this". It aims to hit one of COP31's flagship goals, getting 35% of its energy from electricity, five years early.

And increasingly it is Chinese companies, rather than governments' promises, that are driving the transition. "It's really just a China story," says Li Shuo.

If that is right, it leaves the UK in an uncomfortable place. Hard choices – and they come when household budgets are already stretched thin.

articles.title: I took Vinted to court to get my money back
articles.summary: The BBC hears from Vinted sellers who describe difficulties accessing money held in their online wallets.
articles.body:
Mali Osmelak never imagined that selling clothes on Vinted would end with a court claim to recover almost £6,000.

She started trading on the platform to earn an income while managing Crohn's disease and caring for her four-year-old daughter.

But when she became a professional seller in March, she was unable to complete Vinted's verification process, leaving thousands of pounds inaccessible in her Vinted wallet. After several weeks of trying to resolve the issue, Mali took legal action.

Vinted says sellers may be asked to complete verification checks to comply with legal and regulatory requirements and 98% of transactions are completed smoothly without needing help from its support team.

Vinted is hugely popular in the UK with 17 million users. The online marketplace does not charge a fee to sellers for listing on there.

After the BBC reported on users whose accounts had been suspended or banned , dozens of people got in touch describing difficulties accessing money held in their Vinted wallets.

Mali joined Vinted in 2024 as a side-hustle. Demand for her second-hand gymwear grew rapidly and, within months, she had set up a limited company to expand the business.

This year she signed up for a Vinted Pro seller account - designed for people who want to sell a high volume of items and who are registered as a business.

Within weeks she had generated almost £6,000 in sales. But when she tried to withdraw the money, she discovered her account had been restricted and was told she needed to complete a verification process.

"I thought, 'That's OK. It's not rocket science,'" she says. "I'd set up the business with the help of an accountant and had all the information they needed."

Mali says she spotted an error Vinted had made with her name and she flagged it with Vinted, but "again nothing was done and the verification kept failing". She found herself stuck in a cycle of automated responses.

In an effort to break the deadlock, she also contacted Mangopay, the payments company that at the time operated Vinted sellers' wallets and processed transactions on the platform. She was directed back to Vinted.

After eight weeks without access to the money, Mali decided to take both companies to the small claims court, spending £455 in court fees.

Three days after the court claim was filed, Mali says the account was "magically verified" and she could withdraw the funds.

She still pressed ahead with the case though to try to recover her court fees, costs and interest.

In June, she obtained a default judgement after neither Vinted nor Mangopay responded to her claim, with the court ordering the companies to pay £1,207.50.

But she has yet to receive the money. She has since been informed that Vinted and Mangopay have applied to have the judgement set aside, with a hearing scheduled for December.

"It's been ridiculous and incredibly stressful," she says.

"I need that cash. I will fight it. I'm going to tell the court their system is completely broken. I needed help and nobody helped me."

Vinted said: "Ms Osmelak's check was not successful because her documents did not match the name on her Vinted account. We have since helped her update it, and her account is now verified."

The company did not respond to the BBC's questions about the legal action Mali has taken and continues to pursue.

Mangopay said it was "bound to professional secrecy and data protection obligations. We are, therefore, not allowed to comment on individual cases involving our clients or their users, nor can we share details about specific accounts, transactions or legal matters."

Sportswear seller Azri Mukthar told the BBC he has been trying to withdraw almost £2,500 from his account for over a year.

The businessman was more than happy to become a Pro seller as he was already registered as a limited company.

"I submitted all the documentation they requested and got the go-ahead from Vinted. So then I uploaded all the products and got 30 to 40 sales immediately," he says.

But when he wanted to withdraw his earnings, he found that he couldn't.

"They said my verification was pending," he says.

Azri too, says he's been round in endless circles repeatedly submitting documents only to get an immediate response saying they had been rejected.

"It's frustrating and annoying as there's no clear system to follow.

"You contact customer support and they say you've not submitted X, Y or Z. But I know I have done all they're asking for."

He claims a certificate from Companies House that Vinted requested has been declined 15 times.

Azri has now stopped selling on Vinted and says he is going to have to start legal action.

Vinted said: "Mr Mukthar's check could not be completed because he did not provide all the required documents. Our support team is currently in touch with him to help with his verification."

articles.title: A Haitian 8-year-old was taken by ICE at routine check-in, rattling a San Diego school district
articles.summary: The school district and immigration advocates said the boy was separated from his cousins and uncle, who was taking care of him after his father was deported last year.
articles.body: Wearing a pressed button-down white shirt and slacks, a Haitian boy showed up at a routine immigration appointment in downtown San Diego. Moments later, the neatly dressed 8-year-old was being led away by three immigration officers. As of Monday, his loved ones do not know exactly where he is being held, a California lawmaker said. The scene was captured on a video NBC San Diego obtained Friday. The video was recorded Wednesday by a volunteer observer of immigration proceedings at ICE’s field office. The San Diego Unified School District and members of the Haitian Bridge Alliance, an immigrants rights advocacy group, said the boy was separated from his cousins and uncle, who has been taking care of him after his father was deported last year. Guerline Jozef, executive director of the Haitian Bridge Alliance, said in a statement Monday that even though the uncle followed all the rules, “the child was taken into custody and subsequently transferred to the Office of Refugee Resettlement,” which takes custody of children deemed to be unaccompanied minors. The boy, who has not been identified by name publicly, is a third grader at Fay Elementary School. He was stripped of his immigration protections this summer after a Supreme Court decision allowed President Donald Trump to end Temporary Protected Status for Haitians, according to a letter school district officials sent Friday to the Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the Office of Refugee Resettlement. Temporary Protected Status, better known as TPS, is a humanitarian designation that shielded hundreds of thousands of Haitians from deportation following Haiti’s 2010 devastating earthquake. The protections were renewed multiple times over the years as the Caribbean country sank deeper into crisis. Currently, a majority of the country’s capital is controlled by gangs after the president was assassinated in 2021. After TPS was terminated, the child in San Diego received a letter summoning him to meet with ICE officers last week, school district officials said in their letter. His uncle complied and took him to the appointment “because he did not want to break the law,” added the letter, which NBC News obtained Monday. A DHS spokesperson told NBC San Diego that “a man claiming to be the child’s uncle took him to an ICE check-in.” ICE officers said that they could not confirm the man was related to the boy and that “the alleged uncle could not establish legal guardianship of the minor.” As a result, they determined the boy to be an unaccompanied minor, the DHS spokesperson said. “Out of an abundance of caution and to ensure the child’s safety, ICE determined it was best to remove the child from the household,” the spokesperson said. The Office of Refugee Resettlement told NBC News on Monday that it “does not comment on specific cases” in accordance with its own privacy policies to protect the children in its custody. The third grader is among the 1,640 children considered unaccompanied minors who are under HHS care, according to the agency’s data. Immigration authorities have taken more than 8,000 children into custody over the past year, according to data from the Deportation Data Project. The office of Rep. Juan Vargas, D-Calif., said that the boy’s family does not know where he is being held and that he is helping them obtain the information they need to find him. “Targeting a child, taking them away from their community and classmates, and forcing them into detention is despicable. It is inhumane,” Vargas told NBC San Diego in a statement Friday. “Additionally, TPS protections must be restored for all who’ve had them unfairly ripped away.” DHS has deemed allegations claiming the boy was “placed in detention” as “false.” DHS also said the child was “illegally brought into the United States” at an unspecified time by “a man who alleged to be his father,” who was removed to Mexico by Customs and Border Patrol, not ICE. Jozef said, “His father has already been taken from him and deported, now this administration has stripped him of the stability, family, and community every child deserves.” James Canning, a spokesperson for the school district, told NBC News in a statement on Monday that educators at the boy’s school have pointed to “a general sense of concern for the student’s safety and wellbeing.” School district officials said they are sending additional crisis counselors to Fay Elementary School this week “because the child’s fellow third grade students have expressed concern and fear for their friend.” Canning said no one at DHS or HHS has yet responded to the school district’s letter asking them to reconsider how immigration enforcement policies are affecting students.

images.caption: ICE agents at San Diego's federal building take an 8-year-old Haitian boy into custody on Nov. 4, 2026.

articles.title: Prince William wants more protection for service women from harassment
articles.summary: The Prince of Wales says he wants to stop sexual harassment against women in the armed forces.
articles.body:
The Prince of Wales says more must be done to ensure that women in the armed forces are shown respect and protected from sexual harassment.

Prince William has called for a military culture that is more inclusive and respectful of women - and has warned that at present those values are not always being met.

The prince, who will one day be head of the armed forces, held private meetings with service women for an article he has produced as guest editor of Country Life magazine.

He was told about service women too often facing inappropriate comments, the threat of false rumours and sexual harassment.

Women tell BBC of rape and abuse at Army teen college

Armed forces accused of 'betrayal' over sex abuse

Hundreds of women allege army medical abuse

"I want to play my part in making the military feel like the welcoming, open and professional place I enjoyed and make it feel like that for everyone," writes Prince William, in his first intervention on this subject.

"At the moment, I don't feel that we meet those standards and, as a former serving officer, I really mind it when those who wear the uniform now don't feel safe, respected or valued."

According to royal sources, Prince William has been holding his own fact-finding meetings with service women of all ranks, across the Army, Royal Navy and the Royal Air Force.

He has now raised some of those concerns about the issues concerning women in the armed forces, in the article he commissioned for Country Life.

It cites a survey from the Ministry of Defence that found 67% of service women had faced unwanted "sexualised behaviour" every year and that 30% had considered leaving the armed forces because of such behaviour.

The article also references the experiences of Royal Artillery Gunner Jaysley Beck, who took her own life at Larkhill Camp in Wiltshire in 2021.

Gunner Beck had faced months of unwanted attention and had reported a sexual assault and an inquest heard about a complaints system that failed to adequately respond.

Earlier this year, four young women told the BBC they were sexually assaulted and harassed at an Army training college for teenagers - the Army Foundation College at Harrogate, North Yorkshire - with one saying she was raped by fellow junior soldiers in an attack that lasted hours.

Prince William says he wants service women to feel proud to be part of the armed forces.

But he heard claims of sexualised bullying, such as making inappropriate comments, rumours being shared about women who turned down sexual advances and late-night harassment in barracks.

One junior service woman described women as being used as "commodities".

The prince's article also emphasises efforts being made to create a more positive culture and to prevent "outdated thinking and behaviour" and it highlights women who have had successful military careers.

And it shows how military kit, such as body armour, has been adapted for women, rather than assuming that the default would always be for male service personnel.

The chief of the defence staff, Air Chief Marshal Sir Richard Knighton, said he knew that the experience of women in the armed forces had "not always been what it should be".

"Where behaviours and attitudes have fallen short of the standards we expect, we must be honest about that and continue to drive change," he said.

articles.title: Early prisoner release: More offenders to leave jail on Tuesday
articles.summary: At least 1,350 offenders have been released from jail early under the scheme so far.
articles.body:
Around 650 more offenders will leave jails in England and Wales on Tuesday in the third phase of the government's plan to end the prison population crisis.

The group will include offenders serving up to three years and two months for their crimes.

Under the new rules, they are leaving jail after serving no more than a third of their sentence behind bars, rather than a half.

At least 1,350 offenders have left jail early since 1 October under the first two waves of the scheme.

By the end of the year officials project that at least 2,500 will have been let out to spend two-thirds of their sentence on a licence in the community.

Tuesday's third stage continues the process of releasing batches of offenders serving increasingly long sentences - culminating next June with those serving more than 12 years.

The cohort will include people convicted of affray, which has a maximum sentence of three years, burglary and fraud.

Some violent offenders convicted of wounding, grievous bodily harm with intent or lower-end firearms charges could also be released.

Offenders convicted of one of more than 70 offences are exempt from the earlier release scheme, including manslaughter, rape, sexual and grooming offences and those on life terms.

Weekly prison population statistics show that the early release programme is having an impact - for now - on the population crisis inside jails.

On Monday the latest release of weekly data showed there were 86,982 people in jail, with enough spare spaces to take in 2,076 additional offenders if needs be.

That is 500 more cells available at any one time than was the case on the eve of the programme beginning in October.

Victims' groups and survivors have also raised concerns . Refuge, which supports survivors of domestic abuse, told the BBC last month that perpetrators of such abuse were among those being released.

Typically, those being released should expect to be electronically tagged and subject to other monitoring conditions for the second third of their sentence.

Once outside, they will be monitored by probation officers, who are responsible for trying to make sure that offenders take part in courses or other programmes to turn around their lives - and also that they keep to their licence conditions, which can include bans on entering certain areas and contacting victims.

The government has not yet published any figures for the rate of recall of prisoners to jails for breaching their licence conditions.

The most up to date statistics show that just 12,338 offenders were sent back to jail for breaching their terms between April and June. That was 12% higher than the year before but a decrease on the first three months of the year.

Rehabilitation experts say that the recalls are often more likely to be linked to the offender failing to keep to appointments or living at a specific address. Around a fifth of recalls are for a new offence.

Napo, the probation service union, has previously said the releases have put enormous strain on its members who are charged with monitoring the offenders in the community.

Its members have been balloted over recent weeks on potential strike action over pay and conditions - and the result of that poll is expected on Friday.

The government has offered probation officers a 5% pay rise by the Ministry of Justice, while it had demanded 12% as part of a plan to make up for loss of earnings caused by cuts from 2010.

The Ministry of Justice says the offer is fair and has been accepted by two other unions and is twinned with a £700m investment in probation to recruit 1,300 extra officers and the roll-out of AI tools to cut the workload of monitoring offenders.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has previously criticised the scheme, saying she was "worried about dangerous people being let out on the street when they haven't served their sentence, haven't been rehabilitated".

An early release programme introduced by the Conservatives saw more than 10,000 prisoners freed early between October 2023 and September 2024.

articles.title: Our 373 is their 1,747: How official AQI differs from other methodologies
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Social media is flooded with screenshots of some apps showing Delhi's AQI touching 1,500 to 1,800 on Diwali night even as the city's official
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Social media is flooded with screenshots of some apps showing Delhi's AQI touching 1,500 to 1,800 on Diwali night even as the city's official AQI shared by the Central Pollution Control Board remains below 400.While CPCB has capped Delhi's AQI at 500, other apps, which follow the US's Environmental Protection Agency and WHO's methodology, have no such bar. TOI explains the breakpoint tables of methodologiesAQI at 12 am on Nov 9CPCB (India): 373IAQIR (Swiss firm, uses US method): 214AQI Live-US (Also has India option): 1,747AQI on 1pm on Nov 9CPCB: 360IAQIR: 163AQI Live-US: 217How AQI is calculatedThe Air Quality Index is determined by monitoring the levels of major air pollutants, such as:Particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10)Ground-level ozone (O₃)Carbon monoxide (CO)Sulfur dioxide (SO₂)Nitrogen dioxide(NO₂)For each pollutant, set limits—called breakpoints—help convert its measured level into an AQI score and category.Indian scale: 0–50 (Good) | 100 | 200 | 300 | 400–500 (Severe)US Scale: 0–50 (Good) | 100 | 150 | 200 | 300–500 (HazardouS)India calculates using 24-hr averages, while others use shorter/longer timeframes like hourly avg.For Good, the upper concentration limits are compared. For Severe/Hazardous, comparison is for the concentrations at which those categories begin. Percentages are rounded.A lower threshold means the AQI category is reached at a lower pollutant concentration.Only the 'Good' and 'Severe/Hazardous' categories of the six-category AQI systems are compared for illustrative purposes.NO₂: India uses a 24-hour average; the US uses a 1-hour average. A numerical ratio would be misleading.#Ozone: The US Good value of 0–54 ppb comes from the official EPA 8-hour table. Your image leaves that cell blank because it shows the US 1-hour ozone table instead.At the severe end, different averaging conventions prevent a straightforward comparison.Other factors that cause AQI mismatchCPCB collects raw data from the continuous ambient air quality monitoring stations (CAAQMS).Other apps largely rely on private sensors and use some data of CAAQMS.What CPCB saidAQI calculation methodologies adopted by agencies other than CPCB may have applied breakpoint concentrations that differ from those used in the National Air Quality Index (NAQI).NAQI reported by CPCB is the official AQI for public dissemination in India; other AQI data are not recognised for regulatory or reporting purposes.Various other organisations, global air quality platforms and private entities disseminate AQI data.They fetch information from govt and non-govt sources, including non-regulatory grade instruments, such as low-cost sensors, which have calibration and data quality limitations.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Deadly explosion at Turkey steel factory kills 17 workers, injures 12 others
articles.summary: At least 17 people were killed and 12 others injured in western Turkey in a factory blast on Monday.
articles.body: At least 17 people were killed and 12 others injured in western Turkey in a factory blast on Monday. The explosion ripped through an iron and steel factory, with search and rescue operations continuing amid reports that workers were still trapped under the rubble.The explosion occurred around midday at the Habas Demir Celik plant in the Aliaga district of Izmir province. All those killed and injured were workers at the facility, authorities said.Footage from the scene showed a large fire inside the factory, with thick plumes of smoke and dust rising above the facility. Eyewitnesses said the explosion was so powerful that it shook the ground. One person initially believed an earthquake had struck.The death toll rose to 17 after one of the injured workers, who was in critical condition, died later, Turkey's health minister Kemal Memişoğlu said. "Unfortunately, another of our citizens has lost their life in the explosion at a steel factory in İzmir and the fire that followed, after being in critical condition," he wrote in a post on X.President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan had initially confirmed 16 deaths following a cabinet meeting on Monday, news agency Reuters reported.At least five people have been arrested in connection with the incident, according to a BBC report, citing local media reports.According to initial findings, the blast occurred when a crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed, causing materials to fall into a furnace below. The governor's office said the ceiling crane snapped and fell into an electric arc furnace during the liquid steel casting process, Reuters reported.The explosion took place during scheduled maintenance work at one of the plant's electric arc furnaces, the company that operates the facility said in a statement.Izmir governor Süleyman Elban said some people were believed to remain trapped under the rubble. Search and rescue teams were continuing operations to reach those affected by the blast.The injured workers were taken to hospitals across the region for treatment.Speaking after a cabinet meeting, Erdoğan confirmed the deaths and said investigations into the incident were under way. He also said search and rescue operations were continuing.The Habas plant is located in Aliaga, a major port district of Izmir and one of Turkey's main shipbreaking hubs. articles.title: ‘Zero political aspirations’: UFC chief Dana White responds to Trump’s White House job offer
articles.summary: UFC CEO Dana White on Monday ruled out taking up the vacant White House press secretary position, saying he had “zero political aspirations”, after US
articles.body: UFC CEO Dana White on Monday ruled out taking up the vacant White House press secretary position, saying he had “zero political aspirations”, after US President Donald Trump jokingly suggested that he could take on the role.“I have zero political aspirations,” White told reporters from the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room podium, according to CBS News, putting to rest speculation about a possible move into the Trump administration.White, 56, has headed the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) for more than two decades and is a longtime ally of Trump. He played a prominent role in mobilising support for Trump's 2024 presidential campaign and has frequently appeared alongside the president at public events and rallies. Their association has also extended to UFC events, including one held on White House grounds earlier this year.The clarification came after Trump said on Monday that he was “only kidding” when he floated White's name for the vacant press secretary position. “I will tell you, I was only kidding,” the president told reporters, adding that he had posted pictures of prominent UFC fighters as potential members of White's media team as part of the joke.The speculation began over the weekend when Trump announced on Truth Social that White had been approached for the high-profile communications job. Sharing an AI-generated image of the UFC chief standing behind the White House briefing podium, Trump urged him to accept the position.“Dana, please take the job!” Trump wrote, describing White as a “violent fighter and warrior” and suggesting that he bring in active and retired UFC champions as assistants.“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other,” he added.The post triggered confusion on social media, with some users claiming Trump mistook White for former Pentagon spokesperson Dana W White. articles.title: 5 Indian-origin lawmakers among 19 backing Diwali federal holiday bill in US
articles.summary: Five Indian-American lawmakers have joined 14 other US representatives in backing fresh legislation to designate Diwali as a federal holiday in the United
articles.body: Five Indian-American lawmakers have joined 14 other US representatives in backing fresh legislation to designate Diwali as a federal holiday in the United States. The Diwali Day Act, reintroduced in the House of Representatives under the leadership of Congresswoman Grace Meng, has secured the support of 19 lawmakers and seeks to recognise the festival as an official national holiday.The Indian-origin lawmakers supporting the legislation include Raja Krishnamoorthi, Suhas Subramanyam, Shri Thanedar, Ro Khanna and Ami Bera.Also Read| ‘He won two wars’: Donald Trump rallies behind Hegseth amid impeachment pushGrace Meng, who heads the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), said the legislation would help raise awareness about the festival and promote cultural inclusion."My Diwali Day Act will help educate Americans about the importance of this day, and I will continue working to create a more inclusive nation that honours the rich cultural traditions of its people," she said in an official statement.The proposed legislation describes Diwali, also known as Deepavali or the Festival of Lights, as an important annual observance for several religious communities, including Hindus, Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists. It is also celebrated by billions of people across South Asian, Southeast Asian and Indo-Caribbean communities.Meng said the festival holds different meanings for various religious, ethnic and cultural groups but brings people together through reflection, prayer and gatherings with loved ones."Diwali represents the triumph of good over evil and knowledge over ignorance. At a time when anti-Hindu and anti-South Asian hate is on the rise, recognising Diwali as a federal holiday sends a powerful message that Hindus, as well as Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists, are valued members of our society," she stated.The caucus also pointed to a rise in hostility, intimidation and targeted violence against Hindu and South Asian communities across the country.It cited incidents including vandalism at Hindu places of worship, an attempted mass shooting during Navratri celebrations at a Hindu temple in Illinois, and a recent racist disruption of a Diwali celebration in Washington State."CAPAC has been sounding the alarm that these acts of hate must be taken seriously and investigated by federal authorities," the caucus stated.If passed by Congress, the legislation would make Diwali the 12th federally recognised holiday in the US. Supporters said granting the festival federal holiday status, including a day off, would signal official recognition of the country's diverse cultures and traditions.Meng has also authored the Lunar New Year Day Act, which seeks federal recognition for the Lunar New Year.The Diwali Day Act has received endorsements from several organisations, including Asian Americans Advancing Justice, Asian American Federation, Coalition of Hindus of North America, Hindus for Human Rights, Hindu Temple Society of North America, Indian American Impact, Indian Diaspora Council, Indo-Caribbean Alliance, National Asian Pacific American Bar Association, Sikh American Legal Defence and Education Fund, The Sikh Coalition and Southeast Asia Resource Action Centre, among others.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: TOI photographer Anindya Chattopadhyay's X account was locked after he posted photos & videos showing \"deadly smog\" and poor visibility around
articles.body: NEW DELHI: TOI photographer Anindya Chattopadhyay's X account was locked after he posted photos & videos showing "deadly smog" and poor visibility around NH9 and Lodhi Garden, with the platform citing a "violation of its rules".Chattopadhyay said it was his duty to show "the truth of the post-Diwali situation through my camera".I was only doing my duty, X locked my accountAs Delhi woke up to a thick blanket of post-Diwali smog Monday, I found myself at the centre of an unexpected controversy.My X account was locked after I posted photographs and videos showing poor visibility around NH9 and Lodhi Garden, with the platform citing a “violation of its rules”.I left home at 6.30am and headed towards Akshardham. Near NH9, visibility dropped so sharply that I had to park my scooter on the side of the highway.Standing on a footoverbridge, I began filming the haze. After waiting 15-20 minutes for visibility to improve slightly, I resumed my journey towards Lodhi Garden.The scene there was no better. The city's iconic tombs were barely visible through the dense smog.
